title: Knowledge Gaps and Awareness of Human Papillomavirus and Its Vaccine Among Educated Young Adults in Jordan: A Cross-Sectional Study: A Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract: ABSTRACT Human papillomavirus (HPV) remains a major global public health concern and is strongly associated with cervical and several other cancers. In Jordan, the HPV vaccine has not yet been incorporated into the national immunization program, and public awareness appears limited. We aimed to assess knowledge and attitudes regarding HPV and its vaccine among Jordanian young adults and to examine associations between HPV awareness and sociodemographic factors. A cross‐sectional online survey was conducted among 441 Jordanian adults aged 18–29 years. Participants completed a 35‐item questionnaire adapted from previously validated instruments assessing HPV knowledge, vaccine awareness, beliefs, and attitudes. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and multivariable regression analyses to identify factors associated with HPV knowledge and vaccination status. Overall HPV knowledge was limited (mean score 5.71 ± 4.57 out of 18), and nearly one‐third of participants reported no prior knowledge of the virus. Misconceptions regarding transmission routes and HPV‐related cancers were common. Higher educational level, affiliation with the health sector, and urban residence were independently associated with higher knowledge levels. Vaccination uptake was low (8.2%), and many participants expressed uncertainty regarding vaccine safety and effectiveness. Regression analysis showed that none of the examined variables were significant predictors of vaccination status. In conclusion, Substantial knowledge gaps and uncertainty surrounding HPV vaccination exist among young adults in Jordan. These findings suggest the need for further representative research and may inform future culturally appropriate HPV education efforts. The effectiveness of such approaches in improving HPV vaccine acceptance should be evaluated in future studies.

title: p16 Overexpression and Human Papillomavirus Positivity in More Than 1000 Penile Cancers.
abstract: ABSTRACT Penile cancer is a severe disease, and a large proportion is related to high‐risk (hr) human papillomavirus (HPV). P16 is used as an immunohistochemical marker of HPV in clinical diagnostics. Population‐based data on the prevalence of p16 in penile cancer is scarce. We investigated the prevalence of p16 positivity, and p16 in combination with hrHPV DNA, in a large population of Danish penile squamous cell carcinomas (SCC). Cases diagnosed during 1995–2020 were identified in the Danish Pathology Databank, and tumor samples were tested for HPV DNA (INNO‐LiPA assay). After immunohistochemical p16‐staining, the slides were evaluated by expert pathologists. p16 prevalence was calculated and the combined p16 and hrHPV DNA status (double positivity, double negativity, p16 positive only, and hrHPV DNA positive only) was assessed according to calendar time and histology. Time trends were assessed by calculating estimated annual percentage changes. Of 1028 penile SCCs, 42.8% were p16 positive and 37.8% were double positive. We found no significant changes in prevalences over the study period. The highest prevalence of double positivity was observed in SCCs with HPV‐associated histological features, especially basaloid (63.6%–87.5%). hrHPV genotypes covered by the 9‐valent HPV‐vaccine (HPV16/18/31/33/45/52/58) were detected in 97.9% of double positive SCCs. Based on this large population‐based study, we demonstrate a good correlation between p16 and hrHPV DNA and no substantial changes in the prevalences over time (1995–2020). Nearly all double positive SCCs harbored a hrHPV genotype that could potentially be prevented by vaccination, pointing to a likely future decrease in penile cancer in Denmark.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究纳入了1995年至2020年间诊断的1028例阴茎鳞状细胞癌(SCC),并对肿瘤样本进行了HPV DNA检测和p16免疫组化染色。

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,p16阳性与hrHPV DNA在阴茎鳞状细胞癌中存在强关联性,而9价HPV疫苗覆盖的hrHPV基因型的高阳性率提示通过疫苗接种有可能降低阴茎癌的发病率。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于其观察性质和缺乏随机化。样本量较大,但研究时间相对较短,这可能影响研究结果的普遍适用性。由于研究设计为观察性,且存在潜在的混杂因素,证据强度中等。

analysis_zh.methods: 病例从丹麦病理数据库中识别,肿瘤样本通过INNO-LiPA检测方法进行HPV DNA检测。计算了p16的阳性率,并根据时间顺序和组织学类型评估了p16与hrHPV DNA的联合状态。通过计算估计的年百分比变化来评估时间趋势。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在 1028 个阴茎 SCC 中,42.8% 为 p16 阳性,37.8% 为双阳性。在研究期间没有观察到 患病率 的显着变化。在具有 HPV 相关组织学特征的 SCC 中观察到最高的 患病率 双阳性,尤其是基底细胞样细胞 (63.6%–87.5%)。几乎所有双阳性 SCC 都含有 hrHPV 基因型,该基因型被 9 价 HPV 疫苗 覆盖。

title: Long non-coding RNAs as biomarkers for diagnosis and prognosis in HPV-associated cervical cancer: A systematic scoping review.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) are emerging regulators of HPV-driven carcinogenesis with potential diagnostic and prognostic value in cervical cancer (CC). A contemporary synthesis of clinical and mechanistic evidence is necessary to prioritize candidates for translational development. METHODS: We conducted a systematic scoping review of studies assessing lncRNAs in HPV-associated CC. Searches across major databases yielded 556 records; after de-duplication (n = 220) and screening, 154 full texts were assessed, and 27 studies met the inclusion criteria. No formal quality or risk-of-bias assessment was performed, consistent with the scoping review framework. The extracted data included study identifiers, lncRNA identity, HPV association, sample type/size, expression in HPV-positive disease, diagnostic metrics (AUC/sensitivity/specificity), prognostic measures (survival statistics), and mechanistic findings. RESULTS: The 27 studies described 29 unique lncRNAs, which were upregulated in 75% and downregulated in 25% of the studies. Tissue-derived analyses predominated (21 studies), with cell line experiments in 13 studies and circulating assays in a minority (serum 3; plasma 2). Diagnostic performance was reported in 13/27 studies (∼48%), and prognostic associations were reported in 22/27 (∼81.5%). MALAT1 and GATA6-AS1 were each evaluated in two independent studies, whereas HOTAIR was investigated in two studies with different types of evidence. Mechanistic data consistently implicated HPV E6/E7-dependent regulation, ceRNA/miRNA sponging, cell cycle control, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition. CONCLUSION: The compiled evidence indicates that HPV-responsive lncRNAs represent promising candidate biomarkers for diagnosis and prognosis, and may warrant further investigation as therapeutic targets; however, prospective validation in independent cohorts is required before clinical translation.

elements_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to synthesize clinical and mechanistic evidence on long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) as potential biomarkers for diagnosis and prognosis in HPV-associated cervical cancer, addressing the need for a contemporary review to prioritize candidates for translational development.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: A systematic scoping review was conducted, screening 556 records, de-duplicating to 220, and assessing 154 full texts, resulting in 27 studies meeting the inclusion criteria.
elements_en.methods: Studies assessing lncRNAs in HPV-associated cervical cancer were identified through searches across major databases, with data extracted on lncRNA identity, HPV association, sample type/size, expression in HPV-positive disease, diagnostic metrics, prognostic measures, and mechanistic findings.
elements_en.main_results: Twenty-seven studies described 29 unique lncRNAs, with 75% upregulated and 25% downregulated. Diagnostic performance was reported in 13 studies (48%), and prognostic associations were reported in 22 studies (81.5%).
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that HPV-responsive lncRNAs represent promising candidate biomarkers for diagnosis and prognosis, warranting further investigation as therapeutic targets, but prospective validation in independent cohorts is required.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The compiled evidence indicates that HPV-responsive lncRNAs may serve as promising biomarkers for diagnosis and prognosis in HPV-associated cervical cancer, potentially aiding in surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment strategies.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The review did not perform formal quality or risk-of-bias assessments, and the findings are limited by the lack of prospective validation in independent cohorts.

title_zh: 长非编码 RNA 作为 诊断 的生物标志物和 HPV 相关 宫颈癌 的预后:系统范围界定综述。
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) are emerging regulators of HPV-driven carcinogenesis with potential diagnostic and prognostic value in cervical cancer (CC). A contemporary synthesis of clinical and mechanistic evidence is necessary to prioritize candidates for translational development. METHODS: We conducted a systematic scoping review of studies assessing lncRNAs in HPV-associated CC. Searches across major databases yielded 556 records; after de-duplication (n = 220) and screening, 154 full texts were assessed, and 27 studies met the inclusion criteria. No formal quality or risk-of-bias assessment was performed, consistent with the scoping review framework. The extracted data included study identifiers, lncRNA identity, HPV association, sample type/size, expression in HPV-positive disease, diagnostic metrics (AUC/sensitivity/specificity), prognostic measures (survival statistics), and mechanistic findings. RESULTS: The 27 studies described 29 unique lncRNAs, which were upregulated in 75% and downregulated in 25% of the studies. Tissue-derived analyses predominated (21 studies), with cell line experiments in 13 studies and circulating assays in a minority (serum 3; plasma 2). Diagnostic performance was reported in 13/27 studies (∼48%), and prognostic associations were reported in 22/27 (∼81.5%). MALAT1 and GATA6-AS1 were each evaluated in two independent studies, whereas HOTAIR was investigated in two studies with different types of evidence. Mechanistic data consistently implicated HPV E6/E7-dependent regulation, ceRNA/miRNA sponging, cell cycle control, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition. CONCLUSION: The compiled evidence indicates that HPV-responsive lncRNAs represent promising candidate biomarkers for diagnosis and prognosis, and may warrant further investigation as therapeutic targets; however, prospective validation in independent cohorts is required before clinical translation.
abstract_zh: 背景:长非编码 RNA (lncRNA) 是 HPV 驱动的癌变的新兴调节因子,在 宫颈癌 (CC) 中具有潜在的诊断和预后价值。临床和机械证据的当代综合对于优先考虑转化开发的候选者是必要的。方法:我们对评估 HPV 相关 CC 中 lncRNA 的研究进行了系统范围审查。各大数据库检索共 556 条记录;经过重复数据删除(n = 220)和筛选后,对 154 篇全文进行了评估,其中 27 篇研究符合纳入标准。没有进行正式的质量或偏倚风险评估,这与范围界定审查框架一致。提取的数据包括研究标识符、lncRNA 身份、HPV 关联、样本类型/大小、HPV 阳性疾病中的表达、诊断指标(AUC/敏感性/特异性)、预后指标(生存统计)和机制发现。结果:27 项研究描述了 29 种独特的 lncRNA,其中 75% 的研究上调,25% 的研究下调。组织来源的分析占主导地位(21 项研究),其中 13 项研究采用细胞系实验,少数研究采用循环分析(血清 3 项;血浆 2 项)。13/27 的研究(∼48%)报告了诊断性能,22/27 的研究(∼81.5%)报告了预后关联。MALAT1 和 GATA6-AS1 在两项独立研究中分别进行了评估,而 HOTAIR 在两项具有不同类型证据的研究中进行了调查。机制数据一致表明 HPV E6/E7 依赖性调节、ceRNA/miRNA 海绵作用、细胞周期控制和上皮间质转化。结论:汇总的证据表明,HPV 响应性 lncRNA 代表了 诊断 和预后的有希望的候选生物标志物,并且可能值得作为治疗靶点进行进一步研究;然而,在临床转化之前需要在独立的 队列研究 中进行前瞻性验证。

title: Impact of the HPV vaccination programme on anal HPV infection in gay, bisexual and other men who have sex with men: multi-site enhanced surveillance study in specialist sexual health services in England.
abstract: BACKGROUND: A national human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination programme for gay, bisexual, and other men who have sex with men (GBMSM) in England began in 2016. We evaluated the impact of this programme by monitoring the prevalence of type-specific HPV infections over time. METHODS: Residual rectal swab specimens were collected from GBMSM aged ≤45 years undergoing chlamydia and/or gonorrhoea screening at 10 sexual health services (SHSs) between 2017-19 (Phase 1) and 2021-24 (Phase 2). Specimens were linked to data on sociodemographic characteristics, previous STI diagnoses, and HPV vaccination reported to the UK Health Security Agency's (UKHSA's) national STI surveillance system. Anonymised specimens were tested for type-specific HPV DNA using an in-house multiplex PCR and Luminex-based genotyping test. We compared the prevalence of vaccine-type HPV in each phase, and in those with and without any reported HPV vaccinations. RESULTS: Data from 5,787 rectal swab specimens with HPV testing results were analysed: 3,291 in Phase 1 and 2,496 in Phase 2. There was a 36% decline in the prevalence of anal HPV16/18 infection between Phase 1 and Phase 2. Overall, the prevalence of HPV16/18 was similar in GBMSM with (16.6%; 95% CI 15.2-18.1) and without reported HPV vaccination (15.8%; 95% CI 14.5-17.1). CONCLUSION: Eight years after HPV vaccination of GBMSM began, the prevalence of vaccine-type HPV in GBMSM has declined. Available data did not permit accurate estimation of vaccine effectiveness, likely due to the combined effects of underreporting of vaccinations, herd protection, and bias in vaccination uptake. These findings, albeit ecological, bode well for this targeted programme meeting its aim of reducing HPV-related diseases among GBMSM and reducing health inequalities.

title: Circulating tumor HPV DNA reappearance as an early indicator of recurrence after radiotherapy-based treatment for HPV-associated oropharyngeal cancer: analysis of more than 2000 assessments in 232 patients.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Circulating tumor human papillomavirus DNA (ctHPV DNA) is a promising blood-based surveillance biomarker in HPV-positive oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) and head-and-neck carcinoma of unknown primary (CUP). This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of ctHPV DNA-based molecular testing for detecting disease recurrence. METHODS: Patients with OPSCC/CUP treated at our institution between 2012 and 2024 who had detectable ctHPV DNA in plasma at baseline were included. All patients underwent prospective serial ctHPV DNA surveillance using quantitative PCR. RESULTS: 2928 assessments were performed in 232 patients, including 2192 surveillance tests. Among 220 patients who achieved complete radiologic and molecular response, ctHPV DNA reappearance showed 90.3% sensitivity, 97.9% specificity (Sp), 87.5% positive predictive value (PPV), and 98.4% negative predictive value (NPV) for detecting clinically confirmed recurrence. CtHPV DNA reappearance preceded clinical recurrence in 58.1% of recurrent cases. In per-test interval-based analyses, sensitivity peaked at 90.9% at 45 days, while specificity and NPV remained high (Sp 97.6%-98.8%, NPV ≥ 98.9%) across all time intervals (14-180 days). CtHPV DNA positivity at 1 month after radiotherapy-based treatment completion was strongly associated with worse overall survival (HR 19.1, 95% CI 7.5-48.8) and disease-free survival (HR 15.4, 95% CI 6.7-35.4), whereas the result obtained immediately after treatment had limited prognostic value. CONCLUSIONS: Longitudinal qPCR-based ctHPV DNA monitoring may complement standard post-treatment surveillance in baseline ctHPV DNA-positive HPV-associated OPSCC/CUP by identifying patients at very low short-term risk of recurrence and by providing an early signal of molecular recurrence before clinical confirmation in a subset of patients.

title_zh: 循环肿瘤 HPV DNA 再现作为基于放疗的 治疗 治疗 HPV 相关口咽癌后复发的早期指标:对 232 名患者的 2000 多项评估进行分析。
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Circulating tumor human papillomavirus DNA (ctHPV DNA) is a promising blood-based surveillance biomarker in HPV-positive oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) and head-and-neck carcinoma of unknown primary (CUP). This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of ctHPV DNA-based molecular testing for detecting disease recurrence. METHODS: Patients with OPSCC/CUP treated at our institution between 2012 and 2024 who had detectable ctHPV DNA in plasma at baseline were included. All patients underwent prospective serial ctHPV DNA surveillance using quantitative PCR. RESULTS: 2928 assessments were performed in 232 patients, including 2192 surveillance tests. Among 220 patients who achieved complete radiologic and molecular response, ctHPV DNA reappearance showed 90.3% sensitivity, 97.9% specificity (Sp), 87.5% positive predictive value (PPV), and 98.4% negative predictive value (NPV) for detecting clinically confirmed recurrence. CtHPV DNA reappearance preceded clinical recurrence in 58.1% of recurrent cases. In per-test interval-based analyses, sensitivity peaked at 90.9% at 45 days, while specificity and NPV remained high (Sp 97.6%-98.8%, NPV ≥ 98.9%) across all time intervals (14-180 days). CtHPV DNA positivity at 1 month after radiotherapy-based treatment completion was strongly associated with worse overall survival (HR 19.1, 95% CI 7.5-48.8) and disease-free survival (HR 15.4, 95% CI 6.7-35.4), whereas the result obtained immediately after treatment had limited prognostic value. CONCLUSIONS: Longitudinal qPCR-based ctHPV DNA monitoring may complement standard post-treatment surveillance in baseline ctHPV DNA-positive HPV-associated OPSCC/CUP by identifying patients at very low short-term risk of recurrence and by providing an early signal of molecular recurrence before clinical confirmation in a subset of patients.

title: Prevalence of high-risk human papillomavirus genotypes and associated factors among HIV-infected women in a reproductive age group attending antiretroviral therapy in Nekemte town, Oromia, Ethiopia.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus is a deoxyribonucleic acid virus transmitted primarily sexually. Infection with high-risk human papillomavirus is recognized as the key cause of cervical cancer that is leftover as a public health problem globally. Human immunodeficiency virus infected women of a reproductive age who are on antiretroviral therapy are at higher risk due to debilitated immunity. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the prevalence of high-risk human papillomavirus and associated factors. METHODS: An institutional-based cross-sectional study that included 317 HIV-infected women of a reproductive age group attending antiretroviral therapy was conducted in Nekemte town employing a systematic random sampling technique. A structured questionnaire and record reviews were used to gather the data. Cervical specimens were collected from June to August 2024 and tested at Nekemte Public Health Research and Referral Laboratory using the "Abbott real-time high-risk HPV DNA assay". The collected data were entered into Epi-data version 3.1 and exported to the Statistical Package for Social Sciences version 26 for analysis. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize the data, and logistic regression analyses were performed to identify the determinants. The odds ratio with a 95% confidence interval was computed to assess the presence and degree of association. Following multivariable model fitting, variables with a p-value < 0.05 after adjustment for multiple testing were considered statistically significant. RESULTS: The prevalence of high-risk human papillomavirus was 32.2% [95% CI: 27.1-37.6%], while a single genotype infection with HR-HPV-16, HR-HPV-18 and other HR-HPV accounted for 12.75%, 8.82% and 62.7% respectively. On a multivariate logistic regression, having sex before 18 years (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] =3.54, 95%CI: 1.87-6.69), multiple lifetime sex partners (AOR = 3.69, 95%CI: 1.96-6.96), and a history of sexually transmitted infection (AOR = 3.81, 95%CI: 1.93-7.51) were associated with higher odds of infection. Conversely, a longer duration on antiretroviral therapy was associated with lower odds of infection (AOR = 0.18, 95%CI: 0.06-0.54). CONCLUSION AND RECOMMENDATION: The prevalence was high in the study area. Having multiple sex partners, early sexual debut, history of sexually transmitted infections, and shorter duration on antiretroviral therapy were determinants demanding inclusive intervention efforts. Health authorities hence, need to reinforce routine human papillomavirus screening and health education for human immunodeficiency virus infected women of a reproductive age who are on antiretroviral therapy.

Infection with high-risk human papillomavirus is recognized as the key cause of cervical cancer that is leftover as a public health problem globally. Human immunodeficiency virus infected women of a reproductive age who are on antiretroviral therapy are at higher risk due to debilitated immunity. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the prevalence of high-risk human papillomavirus and associated factors. METHODS: An institutional-based cross-sectional study that included 317 HIV-infected women of a reproductive age group attending antiretroviral therapy was conducted in Nekemte town employing a systematic random sampling technique. A structured questionnaire and record reviews were used to gather the data. Cervical specimens were collected from June to August 2024 and tested at Nekemte Public Health Research and Referral Laboratory using the "Abbott real-time high-risk HPV DNA assay". The collected data were entered into Epi-data version 3.1 and exported to the Statistical Package for Social Sciences version 26 for analysis. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize the data, and logistic regression analyses were performed to identify the determinants. The odds ratio with a 95% confidence interval was computed to assess the presence and degree of association. Following multivariable model fitting, variables with a p-value < 0.05 after adjustment for multiple testing were considered statistically significant. RESULTS: The prevalence of high-risk human papillomavirus was 32.2% [95% CI: 27.1-37.6%], while a single genotype infection with HR-HPV-16, HR-HPV-18 and other HR-HPV accounted for 12.75%, 8.82% and 62.7% respectively. On a multivariate logistic regression, having sex before 18 years (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] =3.54, 95%CI: 1.87-6.69), multiple lifetime sex partners (AOR = 3.69, 95%CI: 1.96-6.96), and a history of sexually transmitted infection (AOR = 3.81, 95%CI: 1.93-7.51) were associated with higher odds of infection. Conversely, a longer duration on antiretroviral therapy was associated with lower odds of infection (AOR = 0.18, 95%CI: 0.06-0.54). CONCLUSION AND RECOMMENDATION: The prevalence was high in the study area. Having multiple sex partners, early sexual debut, history of sexually transmitted infections, and shorter duration on antiretroviral therapy were determinants demanding inclusive intervention efforts. Health authorities hence, need to reinforce routine human papillomavirus screening and health education for human immunodeficiency virus infected women of a reproductive age who are on antiretroviral therapy.

title: Quality Improvement Partnership to Improve Human Papillomavirus Vaccine Rates: Start at Age 9 Campaign.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infections and HPV-related cancers are preventable with vaccination. Initiating the HPV vaccine series at ages 9-10 years is associated with improved vaccination uptake and series completion. This quality improvement (QI) initiative aimed to increase first-dose HPV vaccination rates among 9- to 10-year-olds through the implementation of evidence-based interventions. METHODS: Data were collected from electronic health records (EHRs) of established patients aged 9-10 years with at least 1 documented well-child visit annually from 2021 to 2024. Baseline data were obtained from January 2021 through May 2022. Interventions included provider education, adoption of a system-wide "Start at 9" policy, patient-facing educational materials, and EHR modifications to integrate HPV vaccine orders for patients aged 9 years and older. Monthly vaccination trends were evaluated using a P-chart. RESULTS: A total of 9315 patients aged 9-10 years were included. The percentage of eligible patients receiving their first HPV vaccine increased from a baseline of 2% to 14% following the adoption of the "Start at 9" policy in conjunction with targeted educational interventions and EHR integration. A P-chart demonstrating special cause variation aligned with 2 QI interventions, indicating a sustained process shift. Tetanus, diphtheria, and acellular pertussis (Tdap) vaccination rates, used as balancing measures, remained stable throughout the study period. CONCLUSIONS: A coordinated, systems-level QI approach was associated with significant gains in early HPV vaccine initiation, supporting initiation of vaccination at age 9 years as an effective strategy to promote timely vaccination and strengthen preventive health outcomes.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在通过实施质量改进计划来解决 9 至 10 岁儿童中 HPV 疫苗接种 率低的问题。人乳头瘤病毒 感染和 HPV 相关癌症可以用 疫苗接种 预防。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 开展了一项质量改进计划,通过提供者教育、全系统“从 9 点开始”政策、面向患者的教育材料和 EHR 修改,提高 9 至 10 岁儿童的首剂 HPV 疫苗接种 率。数据收集自 2021 年至 2024 年间每年至少进行过一次健康儿童就诊记录的 9 至 10 岁患者的电子健康记录。
elements_zh.methods: 基线数据从 2021 年 1 月到 2022 年 5 月获得。干预措施包括提供者教育、采用全系统“从 9 点开始”政策、面向患者的教育材料以及修改 EHR 以整合 9 岁及以上患者的 HPV 疫苗 订单。使用 P 图表评估每月 疫苗接种 趋势。
elements_zh.main_results: 共纳入 9315 名 9-10 岁患者。在采用“9 点开始”政策并结合有针对性的教育干预措施和 EHR 整合后,接受首次 HPV 疫苗 的符合资格患者的百分比从 2% 的基线增加到 14%。P 图表显示特殊原因变异与 2 项 QI 干预措施一致,表明持续的流程转变。用作平衡措施的破伤风、白喉和无细胞百日咳 (Tdap) 疫苗接种 率在整个研究期间保持稳定。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 协调的系统级 QI 方法与早期 HPV 疫苗 启动的显着进展相关,支持在 9 岁时启动 疫苗接种 作为促进及时 疫苗接种 和加强预防性健康结果的有效策略。HPV 疫苗接种 率显着增加,并且随着时间的推移持续增加。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,在 9-10 岁时开始 HPV 疫苗 系列与 疫苗接种 吸收和系列完成的改善相关。这种方法可以在其他环境中实施,以提高 HPV 疫苗接种 率并减轻 HPV 相关疾病的负担。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 研究设计的局限性包括缺乏对照组和可能存在混杂因素。由于该研究的观察性质以及数据收集对电子健康记录的依赖,证据强度中等。

Monthly vaccination trends were evaluated using a P-chart. RESULTS: A total of 9315 patients aged 9-10 years were included. The percentage of eligible patients receiving their first HPV vaccine increased from a baseline of 2% to 14% following the adoption of the "Start at 9" policy in conjunction with targeted educational interventions and EHR integration. A P-chart demonstrating special cause variation aligned with 2 QI interventions, indicating a sustained process shift. Tetanus, diphtheria, and acellular pertussis (Tdap) vaccination rates, used as balancing measures, remained stable throughout the study period. CONCLUSIONS: A coordinated, systems-level QI approach was associated with significant gains in early HPV vaccine initiation, supporting initiation of vaccination at age 9 years as an effective strategy to promote timely vaccination and strengthen preventive health outcomes.

title: Human Papillomavirus Status in Penile Squamous Cell Carcinoma: An Established Biomarker With Unanswered Questions.
abstract: Penile squamous cell carcinoma (PSCC) is a rare but aggressive malignancy whose incidence has been rising across several highincome regions in recent decades.A substantial fraction is attributable to high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV).HPV-positive and HPV-negative PSCC differ markedly in tumour biology and in the tumour microenvironment, and most studies report better outcomes for HPV-positive disease-yet the prognostic and therapeutic predictive value of HPV status remains contested and unresolved.Stærk et al. provide a large, high-quality and homogeneous dataset to address these questions: more than one thousand penile SCCs diagnosed in Denmark over 26 years, drawn from the nationwide Danish Pathology Databank with centralised HPV genotyping and blinded expert p16 scoring.

title: Clinicopathologic features and molecular characterization of oropharyngeal carcinomas harboring low-risk human papillomavirus.
abstract: Although the association between high-risk (HR) subtypes of human papillomavirus (HPV) and oropharyngeal carcinoma (OC) is well established, the role and biologic significance of low-risk (LR) HPV in these tumors remains poorly understood. In this series, we present 4 OCs with LR-HPV positivity by in situ hybridization (ISH). The cases occurred in 3 males and 1 female with a mean age of 67.8 years. All tumors demonstrated a papillary/exophytic architecture, and 2 showed overt stromal invasion. Morphologically, the tumors exhibited a spectrum ranging from keratinizing neoplasms with relatively low-grade cytologic features to predominantly non-keratinizing tumors with higher-grade cytology. Glandular differentiation was identified in one case. Koilocytic change was present in all tumors, while prominent intraepithelial neutrophils were identified in two cases. A possible squamous papilloma precursor lesion was present in two cases. All tumors were positive for LR-HPV RNA ISH and negative for HR-HPV RNA ISH. p16 immunohistochemistry was negative in 3 cases and equivocal in one. HPV6 DNA was confirmed in both tumors subjected to sequencing, which additionally identified alterations involving TERT, PIK3CA, FAT1, KRAS, and EP300. Rare OCs may demonstrate transcriptionally active LR-HPV expression and harbor molecular alterations commonly encountered in conventional HPV-independent squamous cell carcinoma. These tumors exhibit morphologic overlap with squamous papilloma, Schneiderian-like papilloma, adenosquamous carcinoma, mucoepidermoid carcinoma, and DEK::AFF2-rearranged carcinoma. While the significance of LR-HPV in these neoplasms remains uncertain, the findings expand the spectrum of HPV-associated lesions encountered in the oropharynx and provide a foundation for future mechanistic studies.

abstract_zh: 尽管高危型(HR)人乳头瘤病毒(人乳头瘤病毒,HPV)与口咽癌(OC)的关联已得到充分证实,但低危型(LR)HPV在这些肿瘤中的作用及其生物学意义仍不明确。在本研究中,我们报道了4例通过原位杂交(ISH)检测出LR-HPV阳性的OC病例。这些病例发生于3名男性和1名女性,平均年龄为67.8岁。所有肿瘤均表现出乳头状/外生性结构,其中2例显示明显的间质浸润。形态学上,肿瘤表现出从具有相对低级别细胞学特征的角化性肿瘤到以非角化性肿瘤为主且具有高级别细胞学特征的广泛谱系。1例肿瘤中观察到腺体分化。所有肿瘤均出现空泡化细胞改变,其中2例观察到显著的上皮内中性粒细胞。2例肿瘤中存在可能的鳞状乳头瘤前病变。所有肿瘤均对LR-HPV RNA ISH呈阳性,而对HR-HPV RNA ISH呈阴性。3例肿瘤的p16免疫组化呈阴性,1例呈不确定。对两例肿瘤进行测序后确认了HPV6 DNA的存在,测序还发现了涉及TERT、PIK3CA、FAT1、KRAS和EP300的改变。罕见的OC可能表现出转录活性的LR-HPV表达,并携带在传统HPV独立鳞状细胞癌中常见的分子改变。这些肿瘤在形态学上与鳞状乳头瘤、类似Schneiderian的乳头瘤、腺鳞癌、黏液表皮样癌以及DEK::AFF2重排癌存在重叠。尽管LR-HPV在这些肿瘤中的意义尚不明确,但这些发现扩展了在口咽部遇到的HPV相关病变的谱系,并为未来机制研究奠定了基础。

title: DNA Methylation Triage after High-Risk Human Papillomavirus Detection: A Critical Narrative Review of Oncogenic Risk Stratification and Precision Cervical Cancer Prevention in West Africa
abstract: High-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) DNA testing has transformed cervical cancer screening because it detects infection with substantially greater sensitivity than morphology-based approaches. Its principal limitation is biological: most hrHPV infections do not progress to cancer, so a positive result identifies exposure and persistence risk rather than the molecular state of transformation. DNA methylation testing has emerged as a candidate reflex triage strategy that measures host-cell or viral epigenetic changes associated with advanced transforming lesions and invasive cancer. This critical narrative review evaluates the biological rationale, clinical performance, self-sampling compatibility, longitudinal evidence, and implementation requirements of methylation-based triage, with particular emphasis on West Africa and on women living with human immunodeficiency virus. Literature published principally from 2010 through 30 June 2026 was identified through international and African scholarly sources, supplemented by citation searching and authoritative guidelines. Across heterogeneous assays, methylation generally rises with lesion severity and provides clinically relevant discrimination among hrHPV-positive women. The most mature evidence supports host panels such as FAM19A4/miR124-2 and ASCL1/LHX8, and combined host-viral classifiers such as S5; other panels remain promising but less externally validated. A major translational advantage is the possibility of reflex testing on the same molecular specimen, including self-collected material, thereby reducing dependence on cytology and repeated clinic attendance. Yet assay-specific thresholds, pre-analytical variation, age effects, heterogeneous endpoints, and geographical concentration of validation studies limit direct transfer to West African programmes. Regional studies demonstrate substantial hrHPV prevalence, diverse genotype distributions, practical feasibility of self-sampling and hub-and-spoke molecular services, and a particular need for efficient triage among women living with human immunodeficiency virus. Direct Nigerian methylomic evidence strengthens biological plausibility but is not yet equivalent to prospective clinical triage validation. Methylation testing is therefore best regarded as a precision-oriented triage technology requiring locally calibrated prospective validation, clinical-utility evaluation, affordability analysis, and integration with assured treatment pathways before routine implementation in West Africa.
journal: Journal of Advances in Medicine and Medical Research

title_zh: 高风险 人乳头瘤病毒 检测后的 DNA 甲基化分类:西非致癌风险分层和精确 宫颈癌 预防的批判性叙述回顾
source_body_en: High-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) DNA testing has transformed cervical cancer screening because it detects infection with substantially greater sensitivity than morphology-based approaches. Its principal limitation is biological: most hrHPV infections do not progress to cancer, so a positive result identifies exposure and persistence risk rather than the molecular state of transformation. DNA methylation testing has emerged as a candidate reflex triage strategy that measures host-cell or viral epigenetic changes associated with advanced transforming lesions and invasive cancer. This critical narrative review evaluates the biological rationale, clinical performance, self-sampling compatibility, longitudinal evidence, and implementation requirements of methylation-based triage, with particular emphasis on West Africa and on women living with human immunodeficiency virus. Literature published principally from 2010 through 30 June 2026 was identified through international and African scholarly sources, supplemented by citation searching and authoritative guidelines. Across heterogeneous assays, methylation generally rises with lesion severity and provides clinically relevant discrimination among hrHPV-positive women. The most mature evidence supports host panels such as FAM19A4/miR124-2 and ASCL1/LHX8, and combined host-viral classifiers such as S5; other panels remain promising but less externally validated. A major translational advantage is the possibility of reflex testing on the same molecular specimen, including self-collected material, thereby reducing dependence on cytology and repeated clinic attendance. Yet assay-specific thresholds, pre-analytical variation, age effects, heterogeneous endpoints, and geographical concentration of validation studies limit direct transfer to West African programmes. Regional studies demonstrate substantial hrHPV prevalence, diverse genotype distributions, practical feasibility of self-sampling and hub-and-spoke molecular services, and a particular need for efficient triage among women living with human immunodeficiency virus. Direct Nigerian methylomic evidence strengthens biological plausibility but is not yet equivalent to prospective clinical triage validation. Methylation testing is therefore best regarded as a precision-oriented triage technology requiring locally calibrated prospective validation, clinical-utility evaluation, affordability analysis, and integration with assured treatment pathways before routine implementation in West Africa.
abstract_zh: 高危型HPV(hrHPV)DNA检测已改变了hrHPV筛查,因为它比基于形态学的方法具有更高的灵敏度。其主要限制是生物学上的:大多数hrHPV感染不会进展为癌症,因此阳性结果识别的是暴露和持续感染的风险,而不是转化的分子状态。DNA甲基化检测作为一种候选的反射性分流策略已崭露头角,它测量与高级转化病变和侵袭性癌症相关的宫颈细胞或病毒表观遗传学变化。这项关键的叙述性综述评估了基于甲基化的分流的生物学依据、临床表现、自我采样兼容性、纵向证据和实施要求,特别强调了西非地区以及人类免疫缺陷病毒(HIV)感染者女性的情况。文献主要从2010年至2026年6月30日发表,来源于国际和非洲学术资源,并通过文献引用搜索和权威指南进行补充。在异质性检测方法中,甲基化通常随着病变严重程度而增加,并在hrHPV阳性女性中提供具有临床意义的区分。最成熟的证据支持诸如FAM19A4/miR124-2和ASCL1/LHX8等甲基化面板,以及结合甲基化和病毒分类器的S5等其他面板;其他面板仍具有前景,但外部验证较少。一个主要的转化优势是可以在同一分子样本上进行反射性检测,包括自我采集的样本,从而减少对细胞学检测的依赖和重复就诊的需求。然而,检测特异性阈值、前分析变异、年龄效应、异质性终点以及验证研究的地理集中性限制了其直接应用于西非项目。区域研究显示了显著的hrHPV患病率,多样化的基因型分布,自我采样和中心辐射式分子服务的实用性可行性,以及在HIV感染者女性中特别需要高效的分流策略。直接的尼日利亚甲基组证据加强了生物学上的合理性,但尚未等同于前瞻性临床分流的验证。因此,甲基化检测最好被视为一种以精准为导向的分流技术,在西非地区常规实施前需要进行本地校准的前瞻性验证、临床效用评估、经济可行性分析以及与确保的病毒检测路径整合。

abstract: Background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) nucleic acid-based testing is the preferred method for cervical cancer screening. Leveraging point-of-care (POC) technologies can increase accessibility to screening in resource-limited settings. However, POC technologies are designed for use with fresh specimens and obtaining pre-clinical data to motivate clinical trials can be difficult. A laboratory-based, proof-of-concept evaluation of the Pluslife HPV-16/18/45 Nucleic Acid Test Card on the Pluslife platform (Pluslife Biotech Co, Ltd., Guangzhou, Guangdong, China) was performed on swabs contrived using AccuTrakTM HPV Qualification Panel (SeraCare) reference material, or residual liquid-based cytology specimens, and stored, self-collected, vaginal swab specimens. Pluslife HPV 16/18/45 results were compared to paired BD OnclarityTM HPV (Becton Dickinson) results to provide analytical performance data (positive percentage agreement (PPA), negative percentage agreement (NPA), overall agreement (Cohen’s Kappa), and relative clinical sensitivity and specificity, all reported with 95 percent confidence intervals (95% CI)). The AccuTrakTM and LBC contrived swab reproducibility results were correct for both inter- and intra-day testing (100.0% agreement). In 50 contrived clinical swabs, PPA was 100.0% (95% CI: 88.4, 100.0), NPA was 95.0% (95% CI: 75.1, 99.9), and overall agreement was 95.8% (95% CI: 87.7, 103.9). When stratified by cytology, the relative clinical sensitivity and specificity were 100.0% (100.0, 100.0) and 95.0% (95% CI: 64.4, 140.0) respectively. Amongst 24 self-collected vaginal swabs, the PPA and NPA were 92.3% (95% CI: 64.0, 99.8) and 100.0% (95% CI: 71.5, 100.0) respectively, with overall agreement of 91.7% (95% CI: 75.7, 107.6). Only one error (cartridge fill) was noted in 120 tests performed. This pre-clinical study described methods for using off-label biorepository specimens. The Pluslife HPV 16/18/45 assay showed similar performance to the BD On-clarityTM HPV assay on both contrived and self-collected vaginal swab specimens. These data support further clinical evaluation of the Pluslife HPV 16/18/45 assay as a solution for rapid, POC HPV screening.

source_body_en: Background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) nucleic acid-based testing is the preferred method for cervical cancer screening. Leveraging point-of-care (POC) technologies can increase accessibility to screening in resource-limited settings. However, POC technologies are designed for use with fresh specimens and obtaining pre-clinical data to motivate clinical trials can be difficult. A laboratory-based, proof-of-concept evaluation of the Pluslife HPV-16/18/45 Nucleic Acid Test Card on the Pluslife platform (Pluslife Biotech Co, Ltd., Guangzhou, Guangdong, China) was performed on swabs contrived using AccuTrakTM HPV Qualification Panel (SeraCare) reference material, or residual liquid-based cytology specimens, and stored, self-collected, vaginal swab specimens. Pluslife HPV 16/18/45 results were compared to paired BD OnclarityTM HPV (Becton Dickinson) results to provide analytical performance data (positive percentage agreement (PPA), negative percentage agreement (NPA), overall agreement (Cohen’s Kappa), and relative clinical sensitivity and specificity, all reported with 95 percent confidence intervals (95% CI)). The AccuTrakTM and LBC contrived swab reproducibility results were correct for both inter- and intra-day testing (100.0% agreement). In 50 contrived clinical swabs, PPA was 100.0% (95% CI: 88.4, 100.0), NPA was 95.0% (95% CI: 75.1, 99.9), and overall agreement was 95.8% (95% CI: 87.7, 103.9). When stratified by cytology, the relative clinical sensitivity and specificity were 100.0% (100.0, 100.0) and 95.0% (95% CI: 64.4, 140.0) respectively. Amongst 24 self-collected vaginal swabs, the PPA and NPA were 92.3% (95% CI: 64.0, 99.8) and 100.0% (95% CI: 71.5, 100.0) respectively, with overall agreement of 91.7% (95% CI: 75.7, 107.6). Only one error (cartridge fill) was noted in 120 tests performed. This pre-clinical study described methods for using off-label biorepository specimens. The Pluslife HPV 16/18/45 assay showed similar performance to the BD On-clarityTM HPV assay on both contrived and self-collected vaginal swab specimens. These data support further clinical evaluation of the Pluslife HPV 16/18/45 assay as a solution for rapid, POC HPV screening.

title: Divergent Human Papillomavirus Genotype Spectra in Three Indigenous Communities of Venezuela: Implications for Vaccine Choice and Cervical Screening
abstract: Genotype-resolved data on human papillomavirus (HPV) are almost absent for Venezuelan indigenous populations. We conducted a multi-site cross-sectional study of 260 indigenous women from La Guajira (Wayuu, n = 94), Maniapure (Eñepa, n = 141), and Delta Amacuro (Warao, n = 25), Venezuela. All samples were processed under a single protocol, with real-time PCR resolving 21 genotypes individually; conventional cytology was available in 144 women. Overall HPV prevalence was 55.4% (95% CI 49.3–61.3) and high-risk HPV prevalence was 51.2% (95% CI 45.1–57.2); positivity differed across communities (χ2 = 13.40, df = 2, p = 0.001), reaching 80.0% in Delta Amacuro versus 59.6% in Maniapure and 42.6% in La Guajira. Nineteen genotypes were detected. HPV-31 was the most frequent overall (15.8%), then HPV-16 (11.5%) and HPV-18 (9.2%). The profiles differed markedly between communities: HPV-68 (48.0%) and HPV-56 (40.0%) in Delta Amacuro, HPV-51 (9.6%) in La Guajira, and HPV-31 (20.6%) in Maniapure. Multiple genotypes were found in 51.4% of infected women. Agreement between cytology and qPCR was negligible (Cohen’s κ = 0.056), with a cytology sensitivity of 25.6%. HPV is highly prevalent in these communities; the circulating genotype spectrum extends well beyond HPV-16/18, and cytology alone is not an adequate screening strategy. In conclusion, the nonavalent vaccine is preferred, as it covers 69.4% of infected women of the indigenous community, compared to 30.6% for the bivalent formulation.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the HPV genotype distribution among three indigenous communities in Venezuela: La Guajira (Wayuu), Maniapure (Eñepa), and Delta Amacuro (Warao). It found significant differences in HPV prevalence and genotype spectra across these communities, with Delta Amacuro showing the highest prevalence at 80.0%. The most common genotypes were HPV-31, HPV-16, and HPV-18. The study highlights the need for tailored vaccination strategies, as the nonavalent vaccine covers 69.4% of infected women compared to 30.6% for the bivalent formulation. However, the agreement between cytology and qPCR was negligible, indicating that conventional cytology is not an adequate screening strategy for these communities. The findings suggest that HPV genotype diversity is substantial and that current screening methods may not be sufficient for effective public health interventions.

title_zh: 委内瑞拉三个土著社区中人乳头瘤病毒基因型谱的差异:对疫苗选择和宫颈筛查的启示
source_body_en: Genotype-resolved data on human papillomavirus (HPV) are almost absent for Venezuelan indigenous populations. We conducted a multi-site cross-sectional study of 260 indigenous women from La Guajira (Wayuu, n = 94), Maniapure (Eñepa, n = 141), and Delta Amacuro (Warao, n = 25), Venezuela. All samples were processed under a single protocol, with real-time PCR resolving 21 genotypes individually; conventional cytology was available in 144 women. Overall HPV prevalence was 55.4% (95% CI 49.3–61.3) and high-risk HPV prevalence was 51.2% (95% CI 45.1–57.2); positivity differed across communities (χ2 = 13.40, df = 2, p = 0.001), reaching 80.0% in Delta Amacuro versus 59.6% in Maniapure and 42.6% in La Guajira. Nineteen genotypes were detected. HPV-31 was the most frequent overall (15.8%), then HPV-16 (11.5%) and HPV-18 (9.2%). The profiles differed markedly between communities: HPV-68 (48.0%) and HPV-56 (40.0%) in Delta Amacuro, HPV-51 (9.6%) in La Guajira, and HPV-31 (20.6%) in Maniapure. Multiple genotypes were found in 51.4% of infected women. Agreement between cytology and qPCR was negligible (Cohen’s κ = 0.056), with a cytology sensitivity of 25.6%. HPV is highly prevalent in these communities; the circulating genotype spectrum extends well beyond HPV-16/18, and cytology alone is not an adequate screening strategy. In conclusion, the nonavalent vaccine is preferred, as it covers 69.4% of infected women of the indigenous community, compared to 30.6% for the bivalent formulation.

title: HPV16 Utilizes Phospholipase C(s) for its Genome Egress
abstract: Abstract Nuclear delivery of human papillomavirus (HPV) requires infected cells to undergo mitosis. Incoming HPV DNA is protected by a transport vesicle structure, which becomes unstable post-mitosis. We have previously shown that HPV genome egress takes on average 4 hours post-mitosis completion; thus, we propose that an enzymatic process is involved in degrading this transport vesicle to allow genome egress. Several phospholipase C (PLC) isoforms, including PLCδ3, PLCζ1, and PLCL1, have been previously implicated in HPV infection in large-scale siRNA screens, and the parvovirus VP1 capsid protein has phospholipase enzymatic activity. Therefore, we hypothesized that cellular phospholipases residing in the nucleus mediate egress of the HPV genome from transport vesicles. We utilized siRNA-mediated knockdown and CRISPR/Cas9 knockout techniques to target specific PLC isoforms in both HeLa and HaCaT cell lines. We found that targeting PLC isoforms PLCβ1, β4, δ3, δ4, and γ1 significantly decreased HPV infection in both HeLa and HaCaT cells, as measured using a luciferase-based reporter assay. We also discovered a novel interaction between HPV16 minor protein L2 and PLCs β1, β4, δ1, δ3, and δ4. Furthermore, we observed that knockout of PLCβ4 and δ4 delayed egress of the HPV genome from nuclear membrane-bound vesicles after infection of HeLa cells. We propose that HPV utilizes phospholipase Cs to achieve genome egress from its protective vesicular structure after nuclear delivery. Importance The cellular factors involved in the later stages of HPV entry remain to be elucidated. Previous data gleaned from large-scale siRNA screens implicated the involvement of phospholipases in HPV infection. We expanded upon these findings and discovered that the individual phospholipase C (PLC) isoforms β4 and δ4 are important for HPV infectivity. We further linked the loss of infectivity in PLCβ4- and PLCδ4-deficient cells to a defect in HPV genome release from its transport vesicle, which we demonstrated using our differential staining technique. Furthermore, we discovered a novel interaction between the minor protein L2 of HPV16 and PLC isoforms β1, β4, δ1, δ3, and δ4.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the mechanisms by which human papillomavirus (HPV) achieves genome egress from its transport vesicle after nuclear delivery, addressing a gap in understanding the cellular factors involved in the later stages of HPV entry.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted using siRNA-mediated knockdown and CRISPR/Cas9 knockout techniques in HeLa and HaCaT cell lines to target specific phospholipase C (PLC) isoforms and assess their impact on HPV infection.
analysis.methods: The researchers used siRNA-mediated knockdown and CRISPR/Cas9 knockout to target PLC isoforms and evaluated the effect on HPV infection using a luciferase-based reporter assay. They also employed a differential staining technique to observe genome release from transport vesicles.
analysis.main_results: Targeting PLC isoforms PLCβ1, β4, δ3, δ4, and γ1 significantly decreased HPV infection in both HeLa and HaCaT cells. Knockout of PLCβ4 and δ4 delayed the egress of the HPV genome from nuclear membrane-bound vesicles.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted their findings as evidence that phospholipase C (PLC) isoforms play a critical role in HPV genome egress, and they discovered a novel interaction between HPV16 minor protein L2 and several PLC isoforms.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings provide insights into the molecular mechanisms of HPV genome release, which could inform the development of targeted therapies or interventions aimed at preventing viral spread.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro experiments using cell lines, and the evidence is based on abstract-only data, which may not fully represent in vivo conditions. The confidence in the findings is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the role of phospholipase C (PLC) isoforms in HPV genome egress after nuclear delivery. The researchers used siRNA and CRISPR/Cas9 techniques to knock down specific PLC isoforms in HeLa and HaCaT cells and observed a significant decrease in HPV infection. They also found that knocking out PLCβ4 and δ4 delayed genome release from transport vesicles. A novel interaction between HPV16 minor protein L2 and several PLC isoforms was identified. These findings suggest that PLCs are critical for HPV genome egress, offering potential targets for therapeutic interventions. However, the study is limited to in vitro experiments, and the evidence is based on abstract-only data, which may not fully capture in vivo dynamics. The confidence in the findings is moderate.

abstract_zh: 摘要 人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)的核内递送需要感染细胞经历有丝分裂。进入的HPV DNA由运输囊泡结构保护,在有丝分裂后变得不稳定。我们之前的研究表明,HPV的核内递送后平均4小时后病毒颗粒开始释放;因此,我们推测一种酶促过程参与降解这种运输囊泡,以允许病毒颗粒释放。几种磷脂酶C(PLC)同工酶,包括PLCδ3、PLCζ1和PLCL1,已在大规模siRNA筛选中与HPV感染相关,并且副腺病毒VP1衣壳蛋白具有磷脂酶酶活性。因此,我们假设细胞核内的磷脂酶介导HPV病毒颗粒从运输囊泡中释放。我们使用siRNA介导的敲低和CRISPR/Cas9敲除技术在HeLa和HaCaT细胞系中靶向特定的PLC同工酶。我们发现,靶向PLC同工酶PLCβ1、β4、δ3、δ4和γ1显著降低了HeLa和HaCaT细胞中的HPV感染,这通过基于荧光素酶的报告基因测定进行测量。我们还发现HPV16小蛋白L2与PLC同工酶β1、β4、δ1、δ3和δ4之间存在新的相互作用。此外,我们观察到在HeLa细胞感染后,敲除PLCβ4和δ4会延迟HPV病毒颗粒从核膜结合囊泡中的释放。我们提出,HPV利用磷脂酶C在核内递送后从其保护性囊泡结构中释放病毒颗粒。重要性 HPV进入的后期阶段涉及的细胞因子仍需阐明。先前的大规模siRNA筛选数据表明磷脂酶在HPV感染中发挥作用。我们在此基础上进一步发现,PLC同工酶β4和δ4对于HPV感染至关重要。我们还发现,PLCβ4-和PLCδ4-缺陷细胞中感染性的丧失与HPV病毒颗粒从运输囊泡释放缺陷相关,我们使用我们的差异染色技术证明了这一点。此外,我们还发现HPV16小蛋白L2与PLC同工酶β1、β4、δ1、δ3和δ4之间存在新的相互作用。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨 HPV 人乳头瘤病毒 在核内递送后如何利用磷脂酶 C (PLC) 同工型实现 基因组 脱壳的机制,填补了对 HPV 后期进入阶段涉及的细胞因子理解的空白。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 研究使用 siRNA 干扰和 CRISPR/Cas9 敲除技术在 HeLa 和 HaCaT 细胞系中靶向特定的 PLC 同工型,评估其对 HPV 感染的影响。
analysis_zh.methods: 研究人员使用 siRNA 干扰和 CRISPR/Cas9 敲除技术靶向 PLC 同工型,并使用基于荧光素酶的报告基因测定法评估其对 HPV 感染的影响。他们还使用差异染色技术观察了 HPV 基因组 从运输囊泡的释放。
analysis_zh.main_results: 靶向 PLC 同工型 PLCβ1、β4、δ3、δ4 和 γ1 显著降低了 HeLa 和 HaCaT 细胞中的 HPV 感染。PLCβ4 和 δ4 敲除延迟了 HPV 基因组 从核膜结合囊泡的脱壳。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将他们的发现解释为证据,表明 PLC 同工型在 HPV 基因组 脱壳中发挥关键作用,并发现了 HPV16 小蛋白 L2 与多个 PLC 同工型之间的新型相互作用。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为 HPV 基因组 释放的分子机制提供了见解,可能有助于开发针对病毒传播的靶向疗法或干预措施。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 研究仅限于使用细胞系进行的体外实验,证据基于摘要中的数据,可能无法完全代表体内条件。对发现的信心程度为中等。

title: For couples in assisted reproduction programmes, concurrent male and female infection with human papillomavirus might be associated with a longer time to clinical pregnancy and a lower live birth rate.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: We assessed in a prospective previous study the association between the human papillomavirus (HPV) status of infertile men and the presence of sperm abnormalities (oligospermia, asthenospermia, and/or teratospermia). However, few studies have reported on the impact of HPV infection on pregnancy rates and live birth rates. MATERIALS AND METHODS: from May to October 2021, we prospectively collected clinical, laboratory, and infection-related data (including HPV status) from 461 men consulting for infertility. We subsequently collected the same data on the men's partners, to assess the impact of both male HPV infections and concurrent couple HPV infections on treatment outcomes. Pregnancy outcomes were assessed using the Kaplan-Meier method. RESULTS: 78 couples were screened for HPV infection. The rate of spontaneous and medically assisted pregnancies was higher among couples with an HPV- male than among couples with an HPV+ male (58.7% vs. 37.5%; p=NS), as was the live birth rate (50% vs. The spontaneous and medically assisted pregnancy rate was higher in HPV- couples than in HPV+ couples (60.5% vs. 37.1%; p=0.06), as was the live birth rate (51% vs. However, time to clinical pregnancy was not significatively longer in HPV+ couples than HPV- couples (p=0.05). CONCLUSION: Couples being assessed for infertility should be systematically screened for HPV. Concurrent HPV positivity appears to be associated with a lower likelihood of pregnancy and a lower birth rate.

title: Long-Term Follow-Up After Surgical Treatment of Anogenital and Oropharyngeal Condyloma Acuminata with Simultaneous HPV Vaccination Initiation in Patients with Concurrent HPV-16 or -18 Co-Infection
abstract: Background/Objectives: Persistent infection with high-risk HPV genotypes accounts for the development of a substantial portion of anogenital and oropharyngeal malignancies. Patients with primary and secondary immunodeficiency or those receiving immunosuppressive therapy, including transplant recipients and patients affected by rare diseases, are vulnerable to particularly severe clinical manifestations of infection. While HPV vaccination constitutes primary prevention, patients with HPV-associated disease remain at risk of reinfection or subsequent infection with alternative genotypes following surgical treatment and may benefit from peri-operative vaccination regimens. This study aimed to evaluate long-term outcomes of HPV vaccination following surgical management of condyloma acuminata in patients with concurrent high-risk genotype infection. Methods: 350 patients with condyloma acuminata and HPV-16 or -18 co-infection confirmed by histopathological examination and PCR genotyping (oral cavity, vulva, vagina, penis, anoderma), including a subgroup with primary or acquired immunodeficiency or chronic immunosuppressive regimens, underwent surgical treatment, receiving simultaneous immunization with the first dose (subsequent completion of full regimen over 12 months) of the bivalent Cervarix vaccine (170 patients) or the quadrivalent Gardasil vaccine (180 patients). A follow-up examination, including HPV genotyping (16/18/31/35), was performed after 6 and 12 months following regimen completion. After 36 months, a standard clinical examination was performed, and in doubtful cases, supplemented with genotyping and biopsy/cytology. Observation was continued in subsequent years (5, 10, and >15 years). Results: Condyloma acuminata requiring removal were observed in 5% of the patients in follow-up at 36 months, with no significant statistical difference between vaccine groups. No cellular atypia or malignant transformation in the form of squamous cell carcinoma was observed. Genotyping did not detect HPV-16/18/31/35 infection in the follow-up examinations. Conclusions: In this uncontrolled, single-arm cohort, peri-operative initiation of either the bivalent or quadrivalent HPV vaccine was associated with a low rate of clinically apparent condyloma acuminata recurrence and no detectable HPV-16/18/31/35 infection during follow-up.

Patients with primary and secondary immunodeficiency or those receiving immunosuppressive therapy, including transplant recipients and patients affected by rare diseases, are vulnerable to particularly severe clinical manifestations of infection. While HPV vaccination constitutes primary prevention, patients with HPV-associated disease remain at risk of reinfection or subsequent infection with alternative genotypes following surgical treatment and may benefit from peri-operative vaccination regimens. This study aimed to evaluate long-term outcomes of HPV vaccination following surgical management of condyloma acuminata in patients with concurrent high-risk genotype infection. Methods: 350 patients with condyloma acuminata and HPV-16 or -18 co-infection confirmed by histopathological examination and PCR genotyping (oral cavity, vulva, vagina, penis, anoderma), including a subgroup with primary or acquired immunodeficiency or chronic immunosuppressive regimens, underwent surgical treatment, receiving simultaneous immunization with the first dose (subsequent completion of full regimen over 12 months) of the bivalent Cervarix vaccine (170 patients) or the quadrivalent Gardasil vaccine (180 patients). A follow-up examination, including HPV genotyping (16/18/31/35), was performed after 6 and 12 months following regimen completion. After 36 months, a standard clinical examination was performed, and in doubtful cases, supplemented with genotyping and biopsy/cytology. Observation was continued in subsequent years (5, 10, and >15 years). Results: Condyloma acuminata requiring removal were observed in 5% of the patients in follow-up at 36 months, with no significant statistical difference between vaccine groups. No cellular atypia or malignant transformation in the form of squamous cell carcinoma was observed. Genotyping did not detect HPV-16/18/31/35 infection in the follow-up examinations. Conclusions: In this uncontrolled, single-arm cohort, peri-operative initiation of either the bivalent or quadrivalent HPV vaccine was associated with a low rate of clinically apparent condyloma acuminata recurrence and no detectable HPV-16/18/31/35 infection during follow-up.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Persistent infection with high-risk HPV genotypes accounts for the development of a substantial portion of anogenital and oropharyngeal malignancies.
analysis.study_design_and_population: 350 patients with condyloma acuminata and HPV-16 or -18 co-infection confirmed by histopathological examination and PCR genotyping underwent surgical treatment, receiving simultaneous immunization with the first dose of the bivalent Cervarix vaccine or the quadrivalent Gardasil vaccine.
analysis.methods: Patients received either the bivalent Cervarix vaccine (170 patients) or the quadrivalent Gardasil vaccine (180 patients) during surgical treatment, with subsequent completion of the full regimen over 12 months. Follow-up examinations, including HPV genotyping (16/18/31/35), were conducted after 6 and 12 months, and a standard clinical examination was performed after 36 months, supplemented with genotyping and biopsy/cytology in doubtful cases.
analysis.main_results: Condyloma acuminata requiring removal were observed in 5% of the patients in follow-up at 36 months, with no significant statistical difference between vaccine groups. No cellular atypia or malignant transformation in the form of squamous cell carcinoma was observed. Genotyping did not detect HPV-16/18/31/35 infection in the follow-up examinations.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: In this uncontrolled, single-arm cohort, peri-operative initiation of either the bivalent or quadrivalent HPV vaccine was associated with a low rate of clinically apparent condyloma acuminata recurrence and no detectable HPV-16/18/31/35 infection during follow-up.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that initiating HPV vaccination peri-operatively may reduce the risk of condyloma acuminata recurrence and prevent subsequent infection with HPV-16, -18, -31, or -35 in patients with concurrent high-risk genotype infection.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is uncontrolled and single-arm, which limits the ability to draw definitive conclusions about the efficacy of peri-operative vaccination. analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the long-term outcomes of HPV vaccination initiated peri-operatively in patients with condyloma acuminata and concurrent HPV-16 or -18 infection. A total of 350 patients received either the bivalent Cervarix or quadrivalent Gardasil vaccine following surgical treatment. Follow-up examinations were conducted at 6, 12, and 36 months, with additional genotyping and biopsy/cytology when needed. The results showed a low recurrence rate of condyloma acuminata (5%) and no detectable HPV-16/18/31/35 infection after 36 months. The authors concluded that peri-operative HPV vaccination may be beneficial in reducing recurrence and preventing subsequent infection. However, the study's uncontrolled design limits the strength of the evidence, though the consistent absence of infection provides moderate confidence in the findings.

abstract_zh: 背景/目的:持续感染高危型人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)基因型是生殖器和口咽部恶性肿瘤发生的重要原因。患有原发性或获得性免疫缺陷或接受免疫抑制治疗的患者,包括移植受者和罕见疾病患者,容易出现感染的特别严重临床表现。虽然HPV疫苗接种是主要的预防手段,但HPV相关疾病患者在手术治疗尖锐湿疣后仍面临再次感染或感染其他基因型的风险,可能从术前术后疫苗接种方案中获益。本研究旨在评估在合并高危基因型感染的尖锐湿疣患者中,手术治疗后同时进行HPV疫苗接种的长期结果。方法:350名尖锐湿疣患者,其HPV-16或-18合并感染经组织病理学检查和PCR基因分型确认(包括口腔、外阴、阴道、阴茎和肛周部位),其中一部分患者具有原发性或获得性免疫缺陷或慢性免疫抑制治疗方案,接受了手术治疗并同时接种了第一剂双价Cervarix疫苗(170名患者)或四价Gardasil疫苗(180名患者),后续在12个月内完成完整接种方案。在完成接种方案后6个月和12个月进行随访检查,包括HPV基因分型(16/18/31/35)。在36个月时进行标准临床检查,对可疑病例补充进行基因分型和活检/细胞学检查。观察持续进行至后续的5年、10年和超过15年。结果:在36个月随访中,有5%的患者需要移除尖锐湿疣,且在双价或四价疫苗组之间无显著统计学差异。未观察到细胞异型性或以鳞状细胞癌形式出现的恶性转化。基因分型未在随访检查中检测到HPV-16/18/31/35感染。结论:在这项未控制的单臂研究中,术前术后开始接种双价或四价HPV疫苗与尖锐湿疣临床复发率低及随访期间未检测到HPV-16/18/31/35感染相关。

analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在这项未控制的单臂研究中,术前术后开始接种双价或四价HPV疫苗与尖锐湿疣临床复发率低及随访期间未检测到HPV-16/18/31/35感染相关。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,术前术后开始接种HPV疫苗可能降低尖锐湿疣复发风险,并防止合并高危基因型感染的患者再次感染HPV-16、-18、-31或-35。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究为未控制的单臂研究,这限制了对术前术后疫苗接种有效性的明确结论。然而,长期随访和HPV-16/18/31/35感染的持续缺失为观察到的结果提供了中等程度的信心。

title: Prognostic Impact of Human Papilloma Virus Infection on Cervical Cancer Outcome in Egyptian Referral Center- Retrospective Cohort Study
abstract: Abstract BACKGROUND Cervical cancer remains a major global health challenge. Although p16^INK4a^ (p16) is a well-established diagnostic surrogate marker for high-risk HPV-related carcinogenesis, its prognostic value in invasive cervical cancer remains controversial. This study evaluated the prognostic significance of p16 expression in combination with the 2018 FIGO stage. METHODS A retrospective cohort study was conducted at a single tertiary referral center, including 122 patients with histologically confirmed cervical carcinoma treated between January 2020 and December 2024. Epidemiological and clinicopathological characteristics, with particular emphasis on the 2018 FIGO stage and p16 immunohistochemical expression, were evaluated. Overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS) were analyzed using Kaplan–Meier survival analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression. RESULTS Among the 122 patients, p16 expression was significantly associated with histopathological subtype (p 55 years and FIGO stage IV as independent predictors of poorer survival and increased recurrence. CONCLUSION In cervical cancer, p16 expression was not an independent prognostic marker. Instead, FIGO stage and patient age were the primary predictors of survival and recurrence. Although p16 remains a valuable biomarker for tumor classification, larger prospective studies are needed to better define its prognostic utility.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Cervical cancer remains a major global health challenge. Although p16^INK4a^ (p16) is a well-established diagnostic surrogate marker for high-risk HPV-related carcinogenesis, its prognostic value in invasive cervical cancer remains controversial.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study evaluated the prognostic significance of p16 expression in combination with the 2018 FIGO stage. A retrospective cohort study was conducted at a single tertiary referral center, including 122 patients with histologically confirmed cervical carcinoma treated between January 2020 and December 2024.
analysis.methods: Epidemiological and clinicopathological characteristics, with particular emphasis on the 2018 FIGO stage and p16 immunohistochemical expression, were evaluated. Overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS) were analyzed using Kaplan–Meier survival analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression.
analysis.main_results: Among the 122 patients, p16 expression was significantly associated with histopathological subtype. Age ≥55 years and FIGO stage IV were identified as independent predictors of poorer survival and increased recurrence.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that p16 expression was not an independent prognostic marker. Instead, FIGO stage and patient age were the primary predictors of survival and recurrence.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that FIGO stage and patient age should be prioritized in assessing prognosis for cervical cancer patients. Further research is needed to better define the prognostic utility of p16 in HPV-associated cervical cancer.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and single-center setting. The evidence is moderate as it is based on a single tertiary referral center and does not include prospective data.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the prognostic impact of human papillomavirus (HPV) infection on cervical cancer outcomes in an Egyptian tertiary referral center. It aimed to clarify the role of p16 expression as a prognostic marker in invasive cervical cancer, which remains controversial. A retrospective cohort of 122 patients with histologically confirmed cervical carcinoma was analyzed for clinicopathological features, including p16 immunohistochemical expression and 2018 FIGO stage. The results showed that p16 expression was significantly associated with histopathological subtype, but not an independent predictor of survival or recurrence. Age ≥55 years and FIGO stage IV were identified as independent predictors of poorer outcomes. The authors concluded that FIGO stage and patient age are more critical for prognosis than p16 expression. The study's findings have implications for clinical practice, emphasizing the importance of staging and age in cervical cancer management. However, the study's limitations include its retrospective design and single-center setting, which may affect generalizability. The evidence is moderate due to these constraints.

title_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒感染对埃及转诊中心宫颈癌结局的预后影响-回顾性队列研究
source_body_en: Abstract BACKGROUND Cervical cancer remains a major global health challenge. Although p16^INK4a^ (p16) is a well-established diagnostic surrogate marker for high-risk HPV-related carcinogenesis, its prognostic value in invasive cervical cancer remains controversial. This study evaluated the prognostic significance of p16 expression in combination with the 2018 FIGO stage. METHODS A retrospective cohort study was conducted at a single tertiary referral center, including 122 patients with histologically confirmed cervical carcinoma treated between January 2020 and December 2024. Epidemiological and clinicopathological characteristics, with particular emphasis on the 2018 FIGO stage and p16 immunohistochemical expression, were evaluated. Overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS) were analyzed using Kaplan–Meier survival analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression. RESULTS Among the 122 patients, p16 expression was significantly associated with histopathological subtype (p 55 years and FIGO stage IV as independent predictors of poorer survival and increased recurrence. CONCLUSION In cervical cancer, p16 expression was not an independent prognostic marker. Instead, FIGO stage and patient age were the primary predictors of survival and recurrence. Although p16 remains a valuable biomarker for tumor classification, larger prospective studies are needed to better define its prognostic utility.
abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 宫颈癌 仍是全球主要健康挑战。虽然 p16^INK4a^ (p16) 已被确立为 高危型HPV 相关致癌的诊断替代标志物,但其在侵袭性 宫颈癌 中的预后价值仍有争议。本研究评估了 p16 表达结合 2018 年 FIGO 分期的预后意义。方法 在单一三级转诊中心开展回顾性 队列研究 研究,纳入 2020 年 1 月至 2024 年 12 月期间接受治疗的 122 例组织学确诊的宫颈癌患者。评估流行病学和临床病理特征,特别关注 2018 年 FIGO 分期和 p16 免疫组织化学表达。采用 Kaplan–Meier 生存分析和 Cox 比例风险回归分析总体生存 (OS) 和无病生存 (DFS)。结果 在 122 例患者中,p16 表达与组织学亚型显著相关(p 55 年龄和 FIGO IV 期作为较差生存和复发增加的独立预测因素)。结论 在 宫颈癌 中,p16 表达不是独立的预后标志物。FIGO 分期和患者年龄是生存和复发的主要预测因素。尽管 p16 仍是肿瘤分类的有价值生物标志物,但仍需更大规模的前瞻性研究以进一步明确其预后价值。

title: Case Report: Possible spatially-distinct de novo invasive cervical carcinoma in the setting of isolated persistent HPV16 after ALA-PDT-mediated histological clearance of CIN3
abstract: Background Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 (CIN3) is a high-grade precancer, and 5-aminolaevulinic acid-mediated photodynamic therapy (ALA-PDT) offers a fertility-preserving alternative for young patients. However, complete lesion regression does not eliminate the latent oncogenic risk of persistent HPV16, and real-world evidence of invasive carcinoma arising after long-term loss to follow-up (LTFU) post-PDT remains scarce. This case report aims to share this clinical observation and provide real-world evidence supporting risk-stratified post-treatment surveillance for patients with isolated persistent HPV16 after histological CIN3 remission. Case presentation A 32-year-old parous woman with TZ2 CIN3 at the 9/12 o'clock cervical positions achieved histological remission after two cycles of standardized ALA-PDT, yet retained isolated HPV16 infection. Despite repeated clinical reminders, she discontinued all surveillance for 20 consecutive months. Upon voluntary re-presentation, newly developed invasive squamous cell carcinoma was confirmed at the 6 o'clock position—a cervical quadrant spatially distinct from the original CIN3 lesions. This finding raises the possibility of de novo malignant transformation from persistent HPV16; however, pre-existing occult multifocal disease cannot be excluded in the absence of viral clonality or HPV integration-site molecular evidence. Multimodal staging indicated theoretical eligibility for fertility-sparing radical trachelectomy. Conclusions Isolated persistent HPV16 retains long-term malignant potential despite resolved precancerous lesions, and can drive spatially separate invasive carcinoma. Because this inference is based on a single observational case without supporting molecular data, risk-stratified intensified surveillance should be further validated in larger cohorts. Standardized follow-up adherence interventions are required to prevent irreversible fertility loss and advanced disease secondary to discontinuous monitoring.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study addresses the risk of malignant transformation following the resolution of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 (CIN3) with ALA-PDT, particularly in the context of persistent HPV16 infection.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a case report of a 32-year-old parous woman with TZ2 CIN3 who achieved histological remission after two cycles of ALA-PDT but retained isolated HPV16 infection. She discontinued surveillance for 20 consecutive months before presenting with newly developed invasive squamous cell carcinoma in a spatially distinct cervical quadrant.
analysis.methods: The case was evaluated using multimodal staging to assess eligibility for fertility-sparing radical trachelectomy. The patient's medical history, treatment protocol, and follow-up adherence were reviewed, and the presence of HPV16 was confirmed through clinical and histological assessments.
analysis.main_results: Upon re-presentation, invasive squamous cell carcinoma was confirmed at the 6 o'clock cervical position, which was spatially distinct from the original CIN3 lesions. The patient had isolated HPV16 infection and had discontinued surveillance for 20 months.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors suggest that the invasive carcinoma may have arisen de novo from persistent HPV16 infection, although pre-existing occult multifocal disease cannot be ruled out without molecular evidence of viral clonality or integration sites.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the potential long-term malignant risk associated with isolated persistent HPV16 infection, even after the resolution of CIN3, and underscore the need for continued surveillance to prevent advanced disease and fertility loss.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on a single observational case without supporting molecular data, which limits the strength of the inference. The evidence is considered moderate due to the lack of broader validation in larger cohorts.

analysis.summary_en: This case report describes a 32-year-old woman with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 (CIN3) who achieved histological remission after two cycles of ALA-PDT but retained isolated HPV16 infection. Despite repeated clinical reminders, she discontinued surveillance for 20 months before presenting with invasive squamous cell carcinoma in a spatially distinct cervical quadrant. The authors suggest that the carcinoma may have arisen de novo from persistent HPV16 infection, although pre-existing occult multifocal disease cannot be excluded without molecular evidence. The study highlights the long-term malignant potential of isolated persistent HPV16 infection and the importance of continued surveillance to prevent advanced disease and fertility loss. However, the findings are based on a single case and lack molecular confirmation, limiting their generalizability and evidence strength. The study supports the need for risk-stratified intensified surveillance and adherence interventions for patients with persistent HPV16.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究探讨了在ALA-PDT清除宫颈上皮内瘤变3级(CIN3)后,持续HPV16感染引发恶性转化的风险,特别是在年轻患者中的情况。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究是一项病例报告,研究对象为一位32岁经产妇女,其TZ2 CIN3在两次ALA-PDT治疗后达到组织学缓解,但保留了孤立的HPV16感染。她在停止监测连续20个月后,因新发侵袭性鳞状细胞癌出现在空间上不同的宫颈象限而复诊。
elements_zh.methods: 该病例通过多模式分期评估其是否符合保留生育能力的根治性宫颈切除术的条件。回顾了患者的病史、治疗方案及随访依从性,并通过临床和组织学评估确认了HPV16的存在。
elements_zh.main_results: 复诊时确认在宫颈6点位置出现侵袭性鳞状细胞癌,该位置与原发CIN3病变空间上不同。患者存在孤立的HPV16感染,并已连续20个月停止所有监测。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,侵袭性癌变可能源于持续HPV16感染的原发性恶性转化,但缺乏病毒克隆性或整合位点的分子证据时,不能排除既往隐匿性多灶性病变的可能性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果突显了孤立持续HPV16感染可能带来的长期恶性风险,即使在CIN3缓解后仍需持续进行监测,以防止疾病进展和生育能力丧失。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究基于单一观察性病例,缺乏支持性分子数据,因此限制了推论的强度。由于缺乏更大规模队列研究的验证,证据强度被评估为中等。

abstract_zh: 背景 宫颈上皮内瘤变3级(CIN3)是一种高级别癌前病变,5-氨基乙酰丙酸介导的光动力疗法(ALA-PDT)为年轻患者提供了一种保留生育能力的替代治疗方案。然而,完全病变消退并不能消除持续HPV16感染的潜在致癌风险,且在ALA-PDT治疗后长期失访(LTFU)情况下出现侵袭性癌变的现实证据仍较为有限。本病例报告旨在分享这一临床观察,并提供现实证据支持对孤立持续HPV16感染患者在组织学CIN3缓解后进行风险分层强化监测的策略。病例报告 一位32岁经产妇女,其宫颈9点和12点位置存在TZ2 CIN3,经过两次标准化ALA-PDT治疗后达到组织学缓解,但保留了孤立的HPV16感染。尽管多次临床提醒,她仍连续20个月停止所有监测。在自愿复诊时,发现新发的侵袭性鳞状细胞癌位于6点位置——这一宫颈象限与原发CIN3病变空间上不同。这一发现提示可能由持续HPV16感染引发新的恶性转化;然而,在缺乏病毒克隆性或HPV整合位点的分子证据情况下,不能排除既往隐匿性多灶性病变的可能性。多模式分期显示该患者理论上符合保留生育能力的根治性宫颈切除术的条件。结论 尽管癌前病变已缓解,孤立持续HPV16感染仍具有长期恶性潜能,并可能引发空间上不同的侵袭性癌变。由于该推论基于单一观察性病例且缺乏支持性分子数据,因此对孤立持续HPV16感染患者进行风险分层强化监测的策略仍需在更大规模的队列研究中进一步验证。需要标准化的随访依从性干预措施,以防止因间断监测导致的不可逆生育能力丧失和疾病进展。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究探讨了在ALA-PDT清除宫颈上皮内瘤变3级(CIN3)后,持续HPV16感染引发恶性转化的风险,特别是在年轻患者中的情况。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究是一项病例报告,研究对象为一位32岁经产妇女,其TZ2 CIN3在两次ALA-PDT治疗后达到组织学缓解,但保留了孤立的HPV16感染。她在停止监测连续20个月后,因新发侵袭性鳞状细胞癌出现在空间上不同的宫颈象限而复诊。
analysis_zh.methods: 该病例通过多模式分期评估其是否符合保留生育能力的根治性宫颈切除术的条件。回顾了患者的病史、治疗方案及随访依从性,并通过临床和组织学评估确认了HPV16的存在。
analysis_zh.main_results: 复诊时确认在宫颈6点位置出现侵袭性鳞状细胞癌,该位置与原发CIN3病变空间上不同。患者存在孤立的HPV16感染,并已连续20个月停止所有监测。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,侵袭性癌变可能源于持续HPV16感染的原发性恶性转化,但缺乏病毒克隆性或整合位点的分子证据时,不能排除既往隐匿性多灶性病变的可能性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果突显了孤立持续HPV16感染可能带来的长期恶性风险,即使在CIN3缓解后仍需持续进行监测,以防止疾病进展和生育能力丧失。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究基于单一观察性病例,缺乏支持性分子数据,因此限制了推论的强度。由于缺乏更大规模队列研究的验证,证据强度被评估为中等。

title: First Results of Mass Immunization of Girls Against Human Papillomavirus in Tajikistan
abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) causes 4.5 % of all new cancer cases worldwide, including cervical cancer. Cervical cancer accounts for the vast majority (83 %) of HPV-associated cancers. To evaluate the first results of the immunization campaign against human papillomavirus in girls aged 10–14 years in the context of increasing incidence of cervical cancer in the Republic of Tajikistan. Materials and Methods. The study analyzed statistical data and reports from the Republican Center for Immunoprophylaxis on the progress of HPV immunization in the republic, as well as on the incidence of cervical cancer, obtained from various specialized medical institutions for the period 2014–2025. Results and Discussion . In 2025, 434 new cases of cervical cancer were registered in the Republic of Tajikistan, with a prevalence rate of 4.1 cases per 100,000 women. Over the past five years (2021 to 2025), this rate has increased by 1.5 times. This annual increase is due to the expansion of visual screening coverage under the state program, as well as a possible increase in actual incidence. Since July 2025, the Republic of Tajikistan has become the 53rd country in the WHO European Region to introduce HPV vaccination into its National Immunization Program. The government officially announced the launch of an HPV vaccination campaign for girls aged 10–14 years on October 1, 2025. The preferred vaccination regimen for Tajikistan is the single-dose quadrivalent Gardasil® vaccine, manufactured by Merck & Co. Thanks to collaboration with GAVI, Tajikistan received 623,000 doses of this vaccine. As of October 31, 2025, the number of girls aged 10–14 vaccinated nationwide reached 95.4 % of the target population, or 522,134 girls. The range of vaccination coverage across all regions of the country ranged from 94.9 % to 96.9 %. During the specified period, 48 cases of adverse reactions after immunization against HPV were registered, which amounted to 0.009 %. The most common symptoms were: weakness/malaise (n = 15; 31.25 %); redness of the skin/face (n = 10; 20.8 %); nausea (n = 8; 16.7 %); fainting (n = 7; 14.6 %); increased body temperature (n = 7; 14.6 %) and collapse (n = 5; 10.4 %). Introduction routine HPV vaccination in the National Immunization Schedule of the Republic of Tajikistan is a prudent and strategically important step. Implementing these measures creates the foundation for achieving national and international goals to eliminate cervical cancer and improve the reproductive and public health of women in the country.
