title: Assessing high-throughput surrogate assays for real-world HPV16- and HPV18-specific vaccine immune monitoring: a comparison of PBNA, cCLIA, and IgG
abstract: Introduction Serological monitoring is needed for the real-world evaluation of immune responses after human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination, but the pseudovirion-based neutralization assay (PBNA) is difficult to apply at scale. Methods This study compared PBNA, competitive chemiluminescent immunoassay (cCLIA), and a virus-like particle-based indirect IgG immunoassay for HPV16- and HPV18-specific antibody assessment. The cross-sectional component included fully vaccinated recipients and unvaccinated controls, while the longitudinal component included adolescent girls receiving a two-dose bivalent HPV vaccine. Correlation, classification performance, systematic bias, and agreement were evaluated. Results All three assays reflected HPV16/HPV18-specific vaccine-induced antibody response trends. cCLIA showed a more stable relationship with PBNA results than the IgG assay, especially in longitudinal monitoring and after the second dose. Although the IgG assay showed lower stability than cCLIA for PBNA-defined functional classification, it consistently captured the overall pattern of vaccine-induced antibody responses at the population level. Persistent numerical differences indicated that the high-throughput assays were not directly interchangeable with neutralization titers. Discussion These findings support a stratified strategy for HPV16- and HPV18-specific immune monitoring using PBNA as a functional laboratory reference, cCLIA for high-throughput surrogate assessment, and IgG testing for population-level trend monitoring.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the use of high-throughput surrogate assays for HPV16- and HPV18-specific immune monitoring. It compares PBNA, cCLIA, and IgG assays in a cross-sectional and longitudinal design, involving vaccinated individuals and unvaccinated controls. The results show that all three assays reflect vaccine-induced antibody trends, with cCLIA demonstrating greater stability in longitudinal monitoring. The authors suggest a stratified approach for immune monitoring, using PBNA as a functional reference, cCLIA for high-throughput assessment, and IgG for population-level trends. The study highlights the limitations of direct interchangeability between assays and their potential roles in different contexts. The evidence is moderate due to the study's design and the observed numerical differences.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估高通量替代检测在现实世界 HPV16 和 HPV18 特异性免疫监测中的效用,因为血清学监测对于评估 免疫应答 HPV 疫苗接种 后至关重要,但 PBNA 大规模实施具有挑战性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究包括全面疫苗接种者和未接种疫苗的对照的横断面部分,以及追踪接受两剂二价 HPV 疫苗 的青春期女孩的纵向部分。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究比较了 PBNA、竞争性化学发光免疫分析 (cCLIA) 和基于病毒样颗粒的间接 IgG 免疫分析对 HPV16 和 HPV18 特异性抗体的评估,评估相关性、分类性能、系统偏倚和一致性。
elements_zh.main_results: 所有三种检测均反映了 HPV16/HPV18 特异性 疫苗 诱导的抗体反应趋势,与 IgG 检测相比,cCLIA 显示与 PBNA 结果的关系更稳定,特别是在纵向监测和第二次给药后。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果建议采用分层方法进行 HPV16 和 HPV18 特异性免疫监测,使用 PBNA 作为功能参考,使用 cCLIA 进行高通量评估,使用 IgG 检测进行人群水平趋势监测。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果为 HPV16 和 HPV18 特异性免疫监测的不同检测方法的实际应用提供了见解,这可以为公共卫生领域的 监测 和人群水平趋势分析提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的横断面和纵向部分可能限制其推广性,且持续的数值差异表明高通量检测方法不能直接替代中和抗体滴度,表明证据强度中等。

title: Knowledge, Attitudes, and Acceptance of Human Papillomavirus Vaccination Among Women of Reproductive Age Attending a Tertiary Hospital in Southeast Nigeria
abstract: Background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is a major cause of cervical cancer, particularly in low- and middle-income countries where access to preventive services is limited. Despite the proven effectiveness of HPV vaccination in preventing HPV-related diseases, vaccine uptake remains low in many developing countries. Aims: This study assessed the knowledge, attitudes, and acceptance of HPV vaccination among women of reproductive age attending a tertiary hospital in Southeast Nigeria. Methods: A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among 366 women aged 15 to 49 years attending Abia State University Teaching Hospital, Aba, Nigeria. Participants were selected through a multistage sampling technique. Data were collected using a structured, interviewer-administered questionnaire that assessed sociodemographic characteristics, knowledge of HPV and HPV vaccination, attitudes towards vaccination, and vaccine acceptance. Data were analysed using IBM SPSS Statistics version 26.0, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05. Results: Most respondents were 25 to 34 years old (40.17%), married (52.19%), and had tertiary education (50.27%). Awareness of HPV was reported by 76.78% of participants. Overall, 45.63% demonstrated good knowledge, 37.43% had moderate knowledge, and 16.94% had poor knowledge of HPV vaccination. Social media (47.27%) and the internet (34.43%) were the main sources of information. Positive attitudes towards HPV vaccination were reported by 63.39% of respondents, while 59.29% demonstrated high vaccine acceptance. The distributions of knowledge, attitudes, and acceptance were statistically significant (p < 0.001). Conclusion: Women attending the tertiary hospital demonstrated relatively high levels of knowledge, positive attitudes, and substantial acceptance of HPV vaccination. However, important knowledge gaps regarding vaccine safety, dosage schedules, and potential side effects remain. Strengthening health education and expanding healthcare provider and digital health interventions may further improve vaccine uptake in Southeast Nigeria.

title: Human Papillomavirus Vaccination Uptake and Perceived Barriers among Women Attending Abia State University Teaching Hospital, Aba, Nigeria
abstract: Background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination remains one of the most effective strategies for preventing cervical cancer. However, vaccine uptake among women in many low- and middle-income countries remains suboptimal due to social, economic, and health system challenges. Aim: This study assessed HPV vaccination uptake and perceived barriers among women attending Abia State University Teaching Hospital (ABSUTH), Aba, Nigeria. Methods: A hospital-based descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among 366 women aged 15 to 49 years attending ABSUTH, Aba. Participants were selected using a structured, interviewer-administered questionnaire developed in accordance with the World Health Organisation behavioural and social drivers’ framework. Data on socio-demographic characteristics, HPV vaccination history, perceived barriers, social influences, accessibility, and strategies for improving vaccine uptake were collected and analysed using IBM SPSS Statistics version 26.0. Descriptive statistics, mean scores, percentages, and the chi-square test were used for data analysis, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05. Results: Only 25.68% of respondents had previously received the HPV vaccine, whereas 74.32% had never been vaccinated. Two vaccine doses were the most frequently reported schedule (44.68%). The most important barriers to vaccination were high cost (74.86%; mean = 3.97), fear of side effects (67.49%; mean = 3.72), limited vaccine availability (63.66%; mean = 3.62), inadequate information (61.20%; mean = 3.54), and insufficient healthcare worker discussion (60.93%; mean = 3.50). Government subsidy (86.61%), free vaccination (84.43%), awareness campaigns (83.33%), and improved vaccine availability (82.79%) were the strongest facilitators of vaccine uptake. Significant associations were observed between vaccination uptake and healthcare worker discussion (χ2 = 3.945, p = 0.047), healthcare worker recommendation (χ2 = 21.158, p < 0.001), and peer influence (χ2 = 47.607, p < 0.001). Conclusion: HPV vaccination uptake among women attending ABSUTH was low. Financial constraints, limited access, inadequate information, and poor provider communication were major barriers. Expanding public awareness, subsidising vaccination, and strengthening healthcare worker engagement may substantially improve HPV vaccine uptake.

abstract_original: Background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination remains one of the most effective strategies for preventing cervical cancer. However, vaccine uptake among women in many low- and middle-income countries remains suboptimal due to social, economic, and health system challenges. Aim: This study assessed HPV vaccination uptake and perceived barriers among women attending Abia State University Teaching Hospital (ABSUTH), Aba, Nigeria. Methods: A hospital-based descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among 366 women aged 15 to 49 years attending ABSUTH, Aba. Participants were selected using a structured, interviewer-administered questionnaire developed in accordance with the World Health Organisation behavioural and social drivers’ framework. Data on socio-demographic characteristics, HPV vaccination history, perceived barriers, social influences, accessibility, and strategies for improving vaccine uptake were collected and analysed using IBM SPSS Statistics version 26.0. Descriptive statistics, mean scores, percentages, and the chi-square test were used for data analysis, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05. Results: Only 25.68% of respondents had previously received the HPV vaccine, whereas 74.32% had never been vaccinated. Two vaccine doses were the most frequently reported schedule (44.68%). The most important barriers to vaccination were high cost (74.86%; mean = 3.97), fear of side effects (67.49%; mean = 3.72), limited vaccine availability (63.66%; mean = 3.62), inadequate information (61.20%; mean = 3.54), and insufficient healthcare worker discussion (60.93%; mean = 3.50). Government subsidy (86.61%), free vaccination (84.43%), awareness campaigns (83.33%), and improved vaccine availability (82.79%) were the strongest facilitators of vaccine uptake. Significant associations were observed between vaccination uptake and healthcare worker discussion (χ2 = 3.945, p = 0.047), healthcare worker recommendation (χ2 = 21.158, p < 0.001), and peer influence (χ2 = 47.607, p < 0.001). Conclusion: HPV vaccination uptake among women attending ABSUTH was low. Financial constraints, limited access, inadequate information, and poor provider communication were major barriers. Expanding public awareness, subsidising vaccination, and strengthening healthcare worker engagement may substantially improve HPV vaccine uptake.

abstract_zh: 背景:人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 疫苗接种 仍然是预防 宫颈癌 的最有效策略之一。然而,由于社会、经济和卫生系统的挑战,许多低收入和中等收入国家的女性对 疫苗 的吸收仍然不够理想。目的:本研究评估了在尼日利亚阿巴阿比亚州立大学教学医院 (ABSUTH) 就诊的女性中 HPV 疫苗接种 的摄取情况和感知到的障碍。方法:对 366 名就读阿坝 ABSUTH 的 15 至 49 岁女性进行了一项以医院为基础的描述性横断面研究。参与者是使用根据世界卫生组织行为和社会驱动因素框架开发的结构化、访谈员管理的调查问卷来选择的。使用 IBM SPSS Statistics 26.0 版收集和分析有关社会人口特征、HPV 疫苗接种 历史、感知障碍、社会影响、可及性以及提高 疫苗 吸收策略的数据。使用描述性统计、平均分、百分比和卡方检验进行数据分析,统计显着性设定为p < 0.05。结果:只有 25.68% 的受访者曾接种过 HPV 疫苗,而 74.32% 的受访者从未接种过疫苗。两种 疫苗 剂量是最常报告的方案 (44.68%)。疫苗接种 最重要的障碍是高成本(74.86%;平均值 = 3.97)、担心副作用(67.49%;平均值 = 3.72)、疫苗 可用性有限(63.66%;平均值 = 3.62)、信息不足(61.20%;平均值 = 3.54)以及医护人员讨论不足(60.93%;平均值 = 3.62) 3.50)。政府补贴(86.61%)、免费疫苗接种(84.43%)、宣传活动(83.33%)和提高疫苗可用性(82.79%)是疫苗吸收的最强促进因素。疫苗接种 的吸收与医护人员讨论(χ2 = 3.945,p = 0.047)、医护人员推荐(χ2 = 21.158,p < 0.001)和同伴影响(χ2 = 47.607,p < 0.001)之间观察到显着相关性。结论:参加 ABSUTH 的女性中 HPV 疫苗接种 的摄取率较低。财务限制、准入有限、信息不足以及提供者沟通不畅是主要障碍。扩大公众意识、补贴 疫苗接种 以及加强医护人员的参与可能会大大提高 HPV 疫苗 的吸收率。

title: Geographic and temporal variations in cancer incidence attributable to human papillomavirus infection in China: a population-based study
abstract: Current epidemiological data on cancer incidence attributable to human papillomavirus (HPV) infection in China remain unclear. This study provides an updated assessment of the magnitude of and geographic variability in the incidence of HPV-attributable cancer in China in 2013–2017, temporal trends from 1988 to 2017 and projections to 2032. Data were extracted from the Cancer Incidence in Five Continents Volumes VII – XII . The population-attributable fraction was calculated by multiplying the high-risk HPV prevalence at each anatomical site by the specific biomarker positivity rate in HPV-positive cases. Joinpoint regression and age-period-cohort models were used to quantify temporal age-standardized incidence rate (ASR) trends and age and birth cohort effects, respectively. Bayesian age-period-cohort models were constructed to project the HPV-attributable cancer incidence through 2032. An estimated 68,955 and 3463 HPV-attributable cancer cases were observed among females and males in China in 2013–2017, respectively, with ASRs of 11.20 (95% confidence interval [ CI ]: 10.98–11.41) and 0.52 (0.20–0.82) per 100,000. The most common HPV-attributable cancers were cervical cancer (females; ASR [95% CI ]: 10.92 [10.83–11.00] per 100,000) and laryngeal cancer (males; 0.21 [0.03–0.37] per 100,000). Among the 25 provinces included, the ASRs of HPV-attributable cervical cancer ranged from 6.15 (5.88–6.42) per 100,000 in Beijing to 17.43 (15.84–19.03) per 100,000 in Hunan (2.8-fold difference). The provincial Human Development Index was inversely associated with the cervical cancer incidence in multivariable linear ecological regression analyses. From 1988 to 2017, the ASRs increased for HPV-attributable cervical cancer (females; average annual percent change [AAPC] and 95% CI : 5.89% [2.82–9.06]) and penile and oropharyngeal cancers (males; 1.98% [0.82–3.15] and 9.65% [5.81–13.62], respectively). Substantial increasing risks across successive generations born between 1908 and 1978 were observed for HPV-attributable cervical cancer among females and oropharyngeal cancer in both sexes. Under a counterfactual continuation of historical trends through 2017, without incorporating subsequent vaccination or screening expansion, the ASR of HPV-attributable cervical cancer is projected to reach 19.53 (95% uncertainty interval [ UI ]: 9.99–34.36) per 100,000 in 2028–2032, compared with 10.92 (95% CI : 10.83–11.00) per 100,000 in 2013–2017. In China, the incidence of HPV-attributable cancer varies considerably according to cancer type and geography. These findings highlight the need for region-specific HPV vaccination and cancer screening strategies, particularly in areas with high incidence rates.

analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 本研究突出了在1908年至1978年间出生的连续几代人群中,女性HPV相关宫颈癌和男女双方的口咽癌均显示出显著上升的风险。这些发现为理解中国HPV相关癌症的长期趋势和地理差异提供了新的见解。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现强调了在高发病率地区制定特定区域的HPV疫苗接种和癌症筛查策略的重要性,以应对中国HPV相关癌症日益增长的负担。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究依赖于《癌症在五大洲的发病率》第七至第十二卷的数据,这些数据可能存在质量或完整性方面的局限性。由于预测假设历史趋势持续,未考虑未来疫苗接种或筛查干预,因此证据强度中等。

title: Post-campaign evaluation of the 2025 national human papillomavirus multi-age cohort vaccination campaign in Sierra Leone: a cross-sectional study of coverage, awareness and caregiver attitudes in selected districts
abstract: The introduction of the Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine for girls aged 10 years in Sierra Leone facilitated the rollout of the national Multi-Age Cohort (MAC) campaign in 2025. This study assessed HPV campaign awareness, vaccination coverage, knowledge, attitudes, barriers to vaccination, and factors associated with vaccine uptake among primary caregivers during the MAC campaign. We conducted a community-based cross-sectional study after the 2025 HPV MAC vaccination campaign in 10 purposively selected districts across all 5 administrative regions of Sierra Leone. This study included 2,253 caregivers of girls aged 11–18 years. We verified vaccination status during the interview against vaccination cards. We purposively sampled districts and collected data using a structured questionnaire administered via mobile data collection tools. We assessed knowledge only among caregivers of vaccinated girls ( n = 2,097). We used modified Poisson regression with cluster-robust standard errors as the primary analysis model to identify independent factors associated with vaccination status. Vaccination coverage was 94.8% (2,097/2,213, 95% CI: 93.2–96.1) in the evaluated districts. Composite knowledge among caregivers of vaccinated girls was 61% (1,280/2,097), 57.3% recognised cervical cancer prevention, and 46.0% knew the HPV vaccine is a single dose. Overall, attitudes toward the HPV vaccination and MAC campaign rollout were positive (mean attitude score 4.0/5.0). The post-campaign attitude score (adjusted PR: 1.060; 95% CI: 1.033–1.088, p < 0.001), campaign awareness (adjusted PR: 1.057; 95% CI: 1.013–1.102, p = 0.011), and girl attending school (adjusted PR: 1.193; 95% CI: 1.080–1.318, p < 0.001) were independently associated with vaccination status. Education level was not associated after cluster-robust correction (adjusted PR: 1.005, p = 0.477). Non-uptake was associated with access constraints, time limitations, and safety concerns. The coverage and uptake of the HPV vaccine were high in the surveyed districts. This was associated with increased awareness, post-campaign attitude score, and school attendance. The findings highlight the role of community-based health workers and nurses as central personnel in reaching girls beyond clinics and schools. These findings provide programmatic learning evidence from selected districts to inform planning the transition from campaign to routine immunisation.

title: Epidemiological characteristics, genotype distribution, and viral load profiles of human papillomavirus infection among women in the Taihu region of Suzhou: a retrospective study
abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection exhibits substantial regional heterogeneity; however, large-scale data regarding genotype distribution and viral load characteristics in the Taihu region of Suzhou, China remain limited. This study aimed to investigate the prevalence, genotype spectrum, age-specific infection patterns, and viral load characteristics of HPV infection among women in this region from 2023 to 2025, thereby providing evidence for region-specific prevention and control strategies. A retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted among 23,196 women who underwent HPV testing in the Taihu region of Suzhou between January 2023 and December 2025. Cervical exfoliated cell samples were collected, and 21 HPV genotypes were detected using real-time fluorescence quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR). Among the 23,196 participants, 3,061 tested positive for HPV, yielding an overall infection rate of 13.20%, with no statistically significant difference across the three study years. The age-specific prevalence demonstrated a bimodal distribution, with the highest infection rate observed in women aged ≥ 60 years and the lowest in those aged 40–49 years. The five most prevalent HR-HPV genotypes were HPV52 (2.70%), HPV58 (1.72%), HPV16 (1.35%), HPV39 (1.11%), and HPV56 (0.96%), while HPV53 (1.78%) was the most common low-risk genotype. Women aged ≥ 60 years exhibited significantly higher proportions of high-risk mixed infections and multiple infections compared with other age groups. Viral load distribution varied across age groups, with high viral loads being most common in women aged < 30 years (24.29%) and low viral loads predominating in women aged ≥ 60 years (46.82%). The genotype spectrum identified in this study showed greater concordance with the genotypes targeted by the nonavalent vaccine than with those targeted by the bivalent or quadrivalent vaccines. HPV52, HPV58, and HPV16 were the predominant genotypes detected among women in the Taihu region of Suzhou. Older women had a higher prevalence of HPV positivity, mixed HR-/LR-HPV infection, and multiple-genotype infection, whereas the proportion of low viral load measurements increased with age. The predominant genotype spectrum showed substantial theoretical overlap with the genotypes targeted by the nonavalent vaccine.

abstract_original: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection exhibits substantial regional heterogeneity; however, large-scale data regarding genotype distribution and viral load characteristics in the Taihu region of Suzhou, China remain limited. This study aimed to investigate the prevalence, genotype spectrum, age-specific infection patterns, and viral load characteristics of HPV infection among women in this region from 2023 to 2025, thereby providing evidence for region-specific prevention and control strategies. A retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted among 23,196 women who underwent HPV testing in the Taihu region of Suzhou between January 2023 and December 2025. Cervical exfoliated cell samples were collected, and 21 HPV genotypes were detected using real-time fluorescence quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR). Among the 23,196 participants, 3,061 tested positive for HPV, yielding an overall infection rate of 13.20%, with no statistically significant difference across the three study years. The age-specific prevalence demonstrated a bimodal distribution, with the highest infection rate observed in women aged ≥ 60 years and the lowest in those aged 40–49 years. The five most prevalent HR-HPV genotypes were HPV52 (2.70%), HPV58 (1.72%), HPV16 (1.35%), HPV39 (1.11%), and HPV56 (0.96%), while HPV53 (1.78%) was the most common low-risk genotype. Women aged ≥ 60 years exhibited significantly higher proportions of high-risk mixed infections and multiple infections compared with other age groups. Viral load distribution varied across age groups, with high viral loads being most common in women aged < 30 years (24.29%) and low viral loads predominating in women aged ≥ 60 years (46.82%). The genotype spectrum identified in this study showed greater concordance with the genotypes targeted by the nonavalent vaccine than with those targeted by the bivalent or quadrivalent vaccines. HPV52, HPV58, and HPV16 were the predominant genotypes detected among women in the Taihu region of Suzhou. Older women had a higher prevalence of HPV positivity, mixed HR-/LR-HPV infection, and multiple-genotype infection, whereas the proportion of low viral load measurements increased with age. The predominant genotype spectrum showed substantial theoretical overlap with the genotypes targeted by the nonavalent vaccine.

abstract_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)感染表现出显著的地域异质性;然而,关于中国苏州太湖地区HPV基因型分布和病毒载量特征的大规模数据仍较为有限。本研究旨在探讨该地区2023年至2025年间女性HPV感染的病毒载量、基因型谱、年龄特异性感染模式及病毒载量特征,从而为制定区域特定的预防和控制策略提供依据。本研究为一项回顾性横断面研究,纳入了2023年1月至2025年12月期间在苏州太湖地区接受HPV检测的23,196名女性。收集宫颈脱落细胞样本,并采用实时荧光定量聚合酶链反应(qPCR)检测了21种HPV基因型。在23,196名参与者中,有3,061名检测出HPV感染,总体感染率为13.20%,且三年间的感染率无显著统计学差异。年龄特异性病毒载量呈现双峰分布,≥60岁女性的感染率最高,而40–49岁女性的感染率最低。最常见的五种高危型HPV基因型为HPV52(2.70%)、HPV58(1.72%)、HPV16(1.35%)、HPV39(1.11%)和HPV56(0.96%),而低危型HPV中,HPV53(1.78%)最为常见。≥60岁女性的高危混合感染和多基因型感染比例显著高于其他年龄段。病毒载量在不同年龄段中分布不同,<30岁女性中高病毒载量最为常见(24.29%),而≥60岁女性中低病毒载量占主导(46.82%)。本研究中鉴定的基因型谱与九价疫苗所针对的基因型具有更高的理论一致性,而非二价或四价疫苗。在苏州太湖地区的女性中,检测到的主要基因型为HPV52、HPV58和HPV16。年龄较大的女性HPV阳性率、高危/低危型HPV混合感染率以及多基因型感染率更高,而低病毒载量的比例则随年龄增长而增加。主要基因型谱与九价疫苗所针对的基因型存在显著的理论重叠。

title: New form of HPV18 L1 found in native virions contributes to virion stability and infectivity
abstract: ABSTRACT Current dogma states that papillomavirus virions consist of only one form of the L1 major capsid protein. Human papillomaviruses (HPVs) have been studied using recombinant particles, thereby bypassing the need to grow the virus in a model of differentiating epithelium. Expression vectors engineered to produce L1 utilize a consensus methionine found in many HPV types. However, HPV18 has two additional in-frame methionine residues located 61 and 26 amino acids upstream of the consensus methionine. These methionine residues are excluded from the L1 expression vector used to create the recombinant virus. On the other hand, HPV produced from organotypic raft culture allows virions to be assembled in a differentiating epithelium in the presence of its native promoters and complete genome. Here, we have utilized this system to show that the wild-type HPV18, produced in a more natural setting, translates a larger form of L1 from the upstream methionine, which is 61 amino acid residues upstream from the consensus methionine, and a smaller form from the consensus methionine, with both sizes assembled in the newly formed virion. Ablation of the upstream methionine residue at position 61 altered the virion capsid conformation, and also decreased virion stability and infectivity. IMPORTANCE The present study investigates whether the papillomavirus virions contain more than one isoform of the L1 major capsid protein. By using organotypic raft cultures that mimic the naturally differentiating epithelium, we revealed that wild-type HPV18 expresses and incorporates two distinct L1 isoforms into the virion, including a previously unrecognized longer form translated from an upstream methionine. Our study has further shown that disruption of the upstream methionine impairs virion stability and infectivity, demonstrating that the longer L1 isoform contributes to proper capsid architecture and viral function. These findings offer a new understanding of HPV capsid biology and have significant implications for the future development of HPV vaccines, diagnostics, and antiviral therapies.

title_zh: 在天然病毒颗粒中发现的新形式的HPV18 L1有助于病毒颗粒的稳定性和感染性
source_body_en: ABSTRACT Current dogma states that papillomavirus virions consist of only one form of the L1 major capsid protein. Human papillomaviruses (HPVs) have been studied using recombinant particles, thereby bypassing the need to grow the virus in a model of differentiating epithelium. Expression vectors engineered to produce L1 utilize a consensus methionine found in many HPV types. However, HPV18 has two additional in-frame methionine residues located 61 and 26 amino acids upstream of the consensus methionine. These methionine residues are excluded from the L1 expression vector used to create the recombinant virus. On the other hand, HPV produced from organotypic raft culture allows virions to be assembled in a differentiating epithelium in the presence of its native promoters and complete genome. Here, we have utilized this system to show that the wild-type HPV18, produced in a more natural setting, translates a larger form of L1 from the upstream methionine, which is 61 amino acid residues upstream from the consensus methionine, and a smaller form from the consensus methionine, with both sizes assembled in the newly formed virion. Ablation of the upstream methionine residue at position 61 altered the virion capsid conformation, and also decreased virion stability and infectivity. IMPORTANCE The present study investigates whether the papillomavirus virions contain more than one isoform of the L1 major capsid protein. By using organotypic raft cultures that mimic the naturally differentiating epithelium, we revealed that wild-type HPV18 expresses and incorporates two distinct L1 isoforms into the virion, including a previously unrecognized longer form translated from an upstream methionine. Our study has further shown that disruption of the upstream methionine impairs virion stability and infectivity, demonstrating that the longer L1 isoform contributes to proper capsid architecture and viral function. These findings offer a new understanding of HPV capsid biology and have significant implications for the future development of HPV vaccines, diagnostics, and antiviral therapies.
abstract_zh: 摘要 当前的教条指出,乳头瘤病毒病毒体仅由 L1 主要衣壳蛋白的一种形式组成。人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 已使用重组颗粒进行了研究,从而绕过了在分化上皮模型中培养病毒的需要。表达 媒介 被设计用于利用许多 HPV 类型中发现的共有蛋氨酸产生 L1。然而,HPV18 有两个额外的框内蛋氨酸残基,位于共有蛋氨酸上游 61 和 26 个氨基酸处。这些甲硫氨酸残基被排除在用于创建重组病毒的 L1 表达 媒介 之外。另一方面,由器官筏培养产生的 HPV 允许病毒粒子在其天然启动子和完整 基因组 存在的情况下在分化的上皮细胞中组装。在这里,我们利用这个系统来证明,在更自然的环境中产生的野生型 HPV18,可以从上游甲硫氨酸(共有甲硫氨酸上游的 61 个氨基酸残基)翻译出较大形式的 L1,以及从共有甲硫氨酸中翻译出较小的形式,两种尺寸都在新形成的病毒体中组装。61位上游甲硫氨酸残基的消融改变了病毒粒子衣壳构象,并且还降低了病毒粒子稳定性和感染性。重要性 本研究调查乳头瘤病毒病毒颗粒是否含有不止一种 L1 主要衣壳蛋白亚型。通过使用模仿自然分化上皮的器官型筏培养物,我们发现野生型 HPV18 表达两种不同的 L1 亚型并将其整合到病毒粒子中,包括从上游甲硫氨酸翻译而来的以前未被识别的较长形式。我们的研究进一步表明,上游蛋氨酸的破坏会损害病毒粒子的稳定性和感染性,证明较长的 L1 亚型有助于适当的衣壳结构和病毒功能。这些发现提供了对 HPV 衣壳生物学的新认识,并对 HPV 疫苗、诊断和 抗病毒药物 疗法的未来发展具有重要意义。

title: Knowledge, Attitude and Practice regarding Human Papillomavirus Infection and HPV Vaccination among Undergraduate Medical Students at a Tertiary Care Teaching Institution in South India: A Cross-sectional Study
abstract: Background: Cervical cancer is an HPV (human papillomavirus) associated disease with India contributing to a disproportionate share of the worldwide burden. Undergraduate female medical students are an at-risk group and future supporters of vaccination yet the gap between knowledge and personal vaccine uptake remains inadequately characterized, especially since India added HPV vaccine to its national immunization campaign. Methods: A questionnaire based cross-sectional study was conducted among all MBBS undergraduates studying in a tertiary care teaching institution in Tamil Nadu using a pre-tested self-administered instrument consisting of sociodemographic items, 15 items of knowledge scale, six items of Likert attitude scale and practice/barrier items. Vaccine coverage was analyzed in female students, the main target population for prevention of cervical cancer. Results: Among the 285 participants, 53.3% were female, and the mean age was 20.3 ± 1.6 years. Good knowledge was present in 172 (60.4%; mean score 10.59 ± 3.78) and a positive attitude in 175 of 277 (63.2%; Cronbach’s α = 0.875). The poorest-answered items concerned the dosing schedule (34.4% correct) and the national-programme status of the vaccine (57.2%). Among female students, self-reported HPV vaccination uptake was 11.8% (18/152), yet 76 of 134 unvaccinated female students (56.7%) were willing to be vaccinated and 80 (59.7%) would accept vaccination after an educational session; the most frequently reported barrier was intention to be vaccinated later (33.3%), followed by lack of information (21.8%). Good knowledge was independently associated with prior awareness of the vaccine (aOR 2.66, 95% CI 1.40–5.04); a positive attitude was less likely in male students (aOR 0.56, 95% CI 0.33–0.94) and more likely with prior vaccine awareness (aOR 1.98, 95% CI 1.04–3.75). Conclusion: Despite moderate-to-good knowledge and favourable attitudes, self-reported HPV vaccination uptake remained low among female MBBS students, highlighting a clear knowledge–practice gap. High willingness to learn and vaccinate suggests that structured education and campus-based vaccination could improve coverage.

title: Post-Treatment High-Risk HPV Testing as a “Test of Cure”: A Systematic Review
abstract: Background/Objectives: Excisional treatment is effective for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or 3 (CIN2–3), but residual or recurrent high-grade disease remains clinically important. This focused systematic review evaluated post-treatment high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) testing as a test of cure and compared it with cytology and resection-margin status. Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE was searched and supplemented by structured citation checking and targeted verification, with supplementary Embase and CENTRAL searches conducted during peer review; the review was not prospectively registered. Mixed-grade cohorts were retained only when a high-grade subgroup was extractable or for supportive qualitative evidence. Results: Fifteen primary studies enrolled 21,932 treated women, of whom 18,992 contributed to endpoint-specific analyses. abstract_zh: 背景/目的:切除性高危型HPV(治疗)对宫颈上皮内瘤变2或3级(CIN2–3)有效,但残留或复发的高级别疾病在临床上仍具有重要意义。本项聚焦系统综述评估了术后高危型HPV(hrHPV)检测作为治愈试验的效用,并将其与细胞学检查和切除边缘状态进行了比较。方法:通过PubMed/MEDLINE进行文献检索,并通过结构化引文核查和针对性验证进行补充;在同行评审期间进行了补充的Embase和CENTRAL检索;本综述未进行前瞻性注册。仅当可提取高级别亚组或用于支持性定性证据时,才保留混合级别高危型HPV(队列研究)的研究。结果:十五项主要研究纳入了21,932名接受治疗的女性,其中18,992名女性参与了终点特异性分析。大多数研究中明确的CIN2+/CIN3+/HSIL+事件发生率为1.9–6.8%,其中一项较早的经过密集验证的高危型HPV(队列研究)研究为11.8%;其他报告中较高的发生率反映了任何级别的CIN或复合结局,并未被视作CIN2+。在报告直接可比准确度指标的子集中,hrHPV检测通常比细胞学检查更具敏感性,其阴性预测值为98.0–100%。这些数值需要谨慎对待,因为复发性高危型HPV(患病率)在某些研究中发生率较低,且组织学验证不完整。五项研究被判定为总体偏倚风险较低,八项为不清楚,两项为较高。结论:现有证据支持基于hrHPV的风险分层以及在检测结果为阴性后进行低强度治疗,但不支持无条件恢复常规人群筛查。需要进行标准化的前瞻性研究,以统一CIN2+终点并实现完整的验证。

title: Prevalence and risk factors of human papillomavirus infection and cervical cytological lesions among women in Shanxi, China: a cross-sectional study
abstract: Abstract Background With the introduction of human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination into China’s national immunization programme in November 2025, robust baseline evidence on HPV epidemiology is critical. Data on HPV prevalence, genotype-specific distribution, risk factors, and the association between HPV infection and cervical cytology will provide a reference for monitoring vaccine impact and optimizing future cervical cancer prevention strategies. Methods We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional study of women undergoing routine health examinations with concurrent HPV DNA testing and cervical cytology between January 2021 to December 2024 in Shanxi, China. We estimated genotype-specific and grouped HPV prevalence, assessed single and multiple infections, and compared genotype distributions across cytological categories. Logistic regression was used to assess factors associated with high-risk (HR-) HPV infection and cytological abnormalities. Results Among 19,384 women (median age 42 years, interquartile range 36–51), HR-HPV prevalence was 10.9%. The most frequent HR-HPV genotypes were HPV52 (2.3%), HPV16 (1.7%), and HPV58 (1.7%). The prevalence of HPV16/18 and HPV6/11/16/18/31/33/45/52/58 was 2.3% and 7.4%, respectively. HR-HPV prevalence was higher in women aged ≥ 56 years (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 2.0, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.6–2.3 for women aged 56–65 years compared to those aged 20–35 years) and lower in married women (AOR = 0.5, 95% CI 0.4–0.7). Abnormal cytology was observed in 2.1% of participants. Among HPV-positive women, HPV16/18 prevalence increased from low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (LSIL) to atypical squamous cells cannot exclude HSIL (ASC-H)/high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL) (OR = 3.4, 95% CI 1.0–11.5), while HPV31/33/45/52/58 prevalence showed a moderate but non-significant increase (1.8, 95% CI 0.6–5.6). Non-16/18/31/33/45/52/58 HR-HPV genotypes decreased with severity (OR = 0.6, 95% CI 0.1–2.2). Conclusions HR-HPV infection was common among women undergoing health examinations in Shanxi with HPV52, HPV16, and HPV58 being the predominant genotypes, and HR-HPV prevalence increased with age. HPV genotype distributions varied substantially across different grades of cytological abnormalities, with HPV16/18 accounting for a larger proportion of high-grade cervical abnormalities. These findings highlight the importance of genotype-specific risk assessment in supporting genotype-specific risk assessment in HPV vaccination and cervical cancer prevention strategies.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study evaluated the prevalence and risk factors of high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) infection and cervical cytological lesions among 19,384 women in Shanxi, China, between 2021 and 2024. HR-HPV prevalence was 10.9%, with HPV52, HPV16, and HPV58 being the most common genotypes. Abnormal cytology was observed in 2.1% of participants, and HPV16/18 was more frequently associated with high-grade cervical abnormalities. The study highlights the importance of genotype-specific risk assessment for HPV vaccination and cervical cancer prevention strategies. However, the cross-sectional design limits the ability to establish causality, and the evidence is considered moderate.

analysis_en.methods: HPV prevalence was estimated using genotype-specific and grouped analysis, and logistic regression was employed to evaluate factors associated with high-risk (HR-) HPV infection and cytological abnormalities.
analysis_en.main_results: High-risk HPV prevalence was 10.9%, with HPV52, HPV16, and HPV58 being the most frequent genotypes. HR-HPV prevalence was higher in women aged ≥ 56 years (AOR = 2.0, 95% CI 1.6–2.3) and lower in married women (AOR = 0.5, 95% CI 0.4–0.7).
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found that HPV genotype distributions varied significantly across different grades of cytological abnormalities, with HPV16/18 accounting for a larger proportion of high-grade cervical abnormalities.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings provide critical baseline data for monitoring the impact of HPV vaccination and inform targeted cervical cancer prevention strategies based on genotype-specific risk assessments.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design, which cannot establish causality, and the potential for confounding factors. The evidence is moderate due to the observational nature of the study.

title_zh: 中国山西省女性患病率及人乳头瘤病毒感染和宫颈细胞学病变的危险因素:一项横断面研究
source_body_en: Abstract Background With the introduction of human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination into China’s national immunization programme in November 2025, robust baseline evidence on HPV epidemiology is critical. Data on HPV prevalence, genotype-specific distribution, risk factors, and the association between HPV infection and cervical cytology will provide a reference for monitoring vaccine impact and optimizing future cervical cancer prevention strategies. Methods We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional study of women undergoing routine health examinations with concurrent HPV DNA testing and cervical cytology between January 2021 to December 2024 in Shanxi, China. We estimated genotype-specific and grouped HPV prevalence, assessed single and multiple infections, and compared genotype distributions across cytological categories. Logistic regression was used to assess factors associated with high-risk (HR-) HPV infection and cytological abnormalities. Results Among 19,384 women (median age 42 years, interquartile range 36–51), HR-HPV prevalence was 10.9%. The most frequent HR-HPV genotypes were HPV52 (2.3%), HPV16 (1.7%), and HPV58 (1.7%). The prevalence of HPV16/18 and HPV6/11/16/18/31/33/45/52/58 was 2.3% and 7.4%, respectively. HR-HPV prevalence was higher in women aged ≥ 56 years (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 2.0, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.6–2.3 for women aged 56–65 years compared to those aged 20–35 years) and lower in married women (AOR = 0.5, 95% CI 0.4–0.7). Abnormal cytology was observed in 2.1% of participants. Among HPV-positive women, HPV16/18 prevalence increased from low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (LSIL) to atypical squamous cells cannot exclude HSIL (ASC-H)/high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL) (OR = 3.4, 95% CI 1.0–11.5), while HPV31/33/45/52/58 prevalence showed a moderate but non-significant increase (1.8, 95% CI 0.6–5.6). Non-16/18/31/33/45/52/58 HR-HPV genotypes decreased with severity (OR = 0.6, 95% CI 0.1–2.2). Conclusions HR-HPV infection was common among women undergoing health examinations in Shanxi with HPV52, HPV16, and HPV58 being the predominant genotypes, and HR-HPV prevalence increased with age. HPV genotype distributions varied substantially across different grades of cytological abnormalities, with HPV16/18 accounting for a larger proportion of high-grade cervical abnormalities. These findings highlight the importance of genotype-specific risk assessment in supporting genotype-specific risk assessment in HPV vaccination and cervical cancer prevention strategies.

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究在中国山西省开展,研究对象为2021年1月至2024年12月期间接受常规健康检查并同时进行HPV DNA检测和宫颈细胞学检查的19,384名女性。
analysis_zh.methods: 通过基因型特异性及分组分析估计HPV 患病率,并采用逻辑回归分析评估高危型(HR-)HPV感染和细胞学异常相关的因素。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 本研究发现,HPV基因型分布因细胞学异常的不同等级而显著变化,其中HPV16/18在高度宫颈异常中占较大比例。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为监测HPV 疫苗接种的影响提供了关键的基线数据,并有助于基于基因型特异性风险评估的针对性宫颈癌预防策略的制定。

title: Diagnostic utility and tissue localization of HPV16 and HPV18 E7 immunohistochemistry in cervical lesion progression: a comparative study with PCR
abstract: Background Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV), particularly HPV16 and HPV18, contributes to cervical carcinogenesis through sustained expression of the viral E7 oncoprotein. Although HPV DNA polymerase chain reaction (PCR) is widely used for viral detection, it does not directly reflect biologically active oncogenic transformation within tissue. This study evaluated the diagnostic utility, clinicopathological significance, tissue localization, and concordance of HPV16 and HPV18 E7 immunohistochemistry (IHC) across the spectrum of cervical lesion progression. Methods A retrospective study was conducted on 109 formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded cervical tissue specimens representing non-neoplastic, premalignant, and malignant lesions. HPV16 and HPV18 E7 protein expression was assessed by immunohistochemistry and compared with HPV DNA PCR findings. Concordance analysis, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and multivariable logistic regression were performed to evaluate diagnostic performance and independent predictive value. Results HPV16 and HPV18 E7 expression increased progressively with lesion severity, with the highest immunoreactivity observed in high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions and invasive carcinoma. Substantial concordance was observed between IHC and PCR findings for both HPV types. HPV16 demonstrated superior diagnostic performance, with sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and area under the curve (AUC) values of 92.3%, 83.9%, 89.9%, and 0.925, respectively, compared with HPV18 (90.0%, 79.3%, 83.7%, and 0.894). Multivariable logistic regression identified HPV16 and HPV18 E7 expression as significant independent predictors of disease status. Histopathological evaluation demonstrated progressive localization patterns, transitioning from focal basal/parabasal staining in low-grade lesions to diffuse full-thickness epithelial and tumor-associated expression in high-grade lesions and invasive carcinoma. Conclusions HPV16 and HPV18 E7 immunohistochemistry demonstrated strong association with cervical lesion severity and substantial concordance with PCR findings, supporting its potential utility as a complementary tissue-based biomarker in cervical pathology. The findings further suggest that E7 immunohistochemistry may provide clinically relevant information regarding biologically active HPV-driven transformation and improve lesion characterization in diagnostically challenging cases.

abstract_zh: 背景 高危 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV),特别是 HPV16 和 HPV18 的持续感染,通过病毒 E7 癌蛋白的持续表达导致宫颈癌发生。尽管 HPV DNA 聚合酶链反应 (PCR) 广泛用于病毒检测,但它并不能直接反映组织内具有生物活性的致癌转化。本研究评估了 HPV16 和 HPV18 E7 免疫组织化学 (IHC) 在宫颈病变进展过程中的诊断效用、临床病理学意义、组织定位和一致性。方法对109例代表非肿瘤、癌前和恶性病变的福尔马林固定石蜡包埋宫颈组织标本进行回顾性研究。通过免疫组织化学评估 HPV16 和 HPV18 E7 蛋白表达,并与 HPV DNA PCR 结果进行比较。进行一致性分析、受试者工作特征(ROC)分析和多变量逻辑回归来评估诊断性能和独立预测价值。结果 HPV16和HPV18 E7表达随病变严重程度逐渐增加,在高级别鳞状上皮内病变和浸润性癌中观察到免疫反应性最高。两种 HPV 类型的 IHC 和 PCR 结果之间观察到显着的一致性。与 HPV18(90.0%、79.3%、83.7% 和 0.894)相比,HPV16 表现出卓越的诊断性能,敏感性、特异性、准确性和曲线下面积 (AUC) 值分别为 92.3%、83.9%、89.9% 和 0.925。多变量逻辑回归将 HPV16 和 HPV18 E7 表达确定为疾病状态的重要独立预测因子。组织病理学评估显示渐进的定位模式,从低级别病变中的局灶性基底/副基底染色转变为高级别病变和浸润性癌中的弥漫性全层上皮和肿瘤相关表达。结论 HPV16 和 HPV18 E7 免疫组织化学显示与宫颈病变严重程度密切相关,并且与 PCR 结果基本一致,支持其作为宫颈病理学中基于组织的补充生物标志物的潜在用途。研究结果进一步表明,E7 免疫组织化学可以提供有关生物活性 HPV 驱动的转化的临床相关信息,并改善诊断困难病例中的病变特征。

title: Multiple High-Risk HPV Infections and Opportunistic HPV Prevalence Among Women Aged 18–25 Years with NILM, ASC-US, or LSIL Cytology: A 2024 Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Multiple high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) infections in young women are poorly characterized across age and cytology, particularly with partial genotyping. We assessed multiple hrHPV infections among HPV-positive women aged 18–25 years with NILM, ASC-US, or LSIL; the secondary objective was hrHPV positivity among electively tested women with NILM. This retrospective cross-sectional study analyzed 2024 laboratory data from northern Slovakia. Of 7613 unique women, 7574 met cytological eligibility criteria; 804 underwent cobas 4800 testing, and 295 were hrHPV-positive. Multiple infection, defined as concurrent detection of at least two reportable categories (HPV16, HPV18, or other hrHPV), occurred in 69/295 women (23.4%; 95% CI, 18.9–28.5%). No statistically detectable variation was observed by cytology after age adjustment (p = 0.471) or by age after cytology adjustment (p = 0.891). Among women with multiple infections, HPV16 combined with other hrHPV was the most frequent pattern (30/69; 43.5%). Among 396 electively tested women with NILM, 75 were hrHPV-positive (18.9%; 95% CI, 15.4–23.1%); positivity was lower at ages 23–25 than 18–22 (10.6% vs. 26.6%; OR, 0.33; 95% CI, 0.19–0.57; p < 0.001). The NILM estimate describes a self-selected preventive cohort and is not population-representative.

analysis.methods: The study used laboratory data from 2024 and applied cobas 4800 testing to identify hrHPV positivity. Multiple infection was defined as concurrent detection of at least two reportable categories (HPV16, HPV18, or other hrHPV).

analysis.summary_en: This 2024 cross-sectional study in northern Slovakia examined multiple high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) infections among women aged 18–25 with NILM, ASC-US, or LSIL cytology. title_zh: 18-25岁女性中多重高危型HPV感染及机会性HPV感染:2024年横断面研究
source_body_en: Multiple high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) infections in young women are poorly characterized across age and cytology, particularly with partial genotyping. We assessed multiple hrHPV infections among HPV-positive women aged 18–25 years with NILM, ASC-US, or LSIL; the secondary objective was hrHPV positivity among electively tested women with NILM. This retrospective cross-sectional study analyzed 2024 laboratory data from northern Slovakia. Of 7613 unique women, 7574 met cytological eligibility criteria; 804 underwent cobas 4800 testing, and 295 were hrHPV-positive. Multiple infection, defined as concurrent detection of at least two reportable categories (HPV16, HPV18, or other hrHPV), occurred in 69/295 women (23.4%; 95% CI, 18.9–28.5%). No statistically detectable variation was observed by cytology after age adjustment (p = 0.471) or by age after cytology adjustment (p = 0.891). Among women with multiple infections, HPV16 combined with other hrHPV was the most frequent pattern (30/69; 43.5%). Among 396 electively tested women with NILM, 75 were hrHPV-positive (18.9%; 95% CI, 15.4–23.1%); positivity was lower at ages 23–25 than 18–22 (10.6% vs. 26.6%; OR, 0.33; 95% CI, 0.19–0.57; p < 0.001). The NILM estimate describes a self-selected preventive cohort and is not population-representative.

title: Recurrence and Circulating Tumor DNA in Human Papillomavirus‐Positive Oropharyngeal Cancer: A Meta‐Analysis
abstract: Abstract Objective To perform a systematic review and meta‐analysis on the utility of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) in serum as a biomarker for post‐treatment surveillance of human papillomavirus (HPV)‐positive oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC), given the improved treatment response and 10% to 20% recurrence rate in this patient population. Data Sources Articles were sourced from PubMed. Studies were excluded if they focused on HPV‐driven cancers in other anatomical regions, lacked pretreatment and posttreatment HPV viral load data, or were published more than 20 years ago. All literature available in English was considered. Review Methods A PRISMA‐compliant review identified 419 articles, and 20 studies met all inclusion criteria. Data extraction and quality assessment were performed using Oxford Centre for Evidence‐Based Medicine and Newcastle‐Ottawa Scale criteria. Results Across 3505 clinically correlated tests, pooled sensitivity was 80.3% (95% CI 70.9%‐87.2%) and specificity was 95.5% (90.9%‐97.8%). Meta‐analysis of our studies found the overall prevalence of recurrent HPV + OPSCC after curative treatment was 9.70% (95% CI 8.72%‐10.78%). Negative Predictive Value (NPV) at this prevalence was 97.7% (96.7%‐98.5%) and Positive Predictive Value (PPV) was 66.0% (49.5%‐80.3%). A positive test for ctDNA after curative treatment had a 130.3 (95% CI 56.60‐298.71) fold higher odds of disease recurrence compared to a negative test. Conclusions CtDNA is a promising biomarker for early detection of recurrence. Standardized protocols and quantitative thresholds are needed to fully establish its role in clinical practice.

abstract_original: Abstract Objective To perform a systematic review and meta‐analysis on the utility of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) in serum as a biomarker for post‐treatment surveillance of human papillomavirus (HPV)‐positive oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC), given the improved treatment response and 10% to 20% recurrence rate in this patient population. Data Sources Articles were sourced from PubMed. Studies were excluded if they focused on HPV‐driven cancers in other anatomical regions, lacked pretreatment and posttreatment HPV viral load data, or were published more than 20 years ago. All literature available in English was considered. Review Methods A PRISMA‐compliant review identified 419 articles, and 20 studies met all inclusion criteria. Data extraction and quality assessment were performed using Oxford Centre for Evidence‐Based Medicine and Newcastle‐Ottawa Scale criteria. Results Across 3505 clinically correlated tests, pooled sensitivity was 80.3% (95% CI 70.9%‐87.2%) and specificity was 95.5% (90.9%‐97.8%). Meta‐analysis of our studies found the overall prevalence of recurrent HPV + OPSCC after curative treatment was 9.70% (95% CI 8.72%‐10.78%). Negative Predictive Value (NPV) at this prevalence was 97.7% (96.7%‐98.5%) and Positive Predictive Value (PPV) was 66.0% (49.5%‐80.3%). A positive test for ctDNA after curative treatment had a 130.3 (95% CI 56.60‐298.71) fold higher odds of disease recurrence compared to a negative test. Conclusions CtDNA is a promising biomarker for early detection of recurrence. Standardized protocols and quantitative thresholds are needed to fully establish its role in clinical practice.

abstract_zh: 摘要 目的 本研究旨在对循环肿瘤DNA(ctDNA)在血清中作为生物标志物用于人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)阳性口咽鳞状细胞癌(OPSCC)患者在根治性治疗治疗后复发的检测价值进行系统综述和荟萃分析,鉴于该患者群体中治疗反应改善且复发率为10%至20%。数据来源 文章来源于PubMed。排除标准包括:研究对象为其他解剖部位的HPV驱动型癌症、缺乏治疗前和治疗后HPV病毒载量数据、或发表时间超过20年的研究。所有英文文献均被纳入考虑。综述方法 采用PRISMA合规的综述方法,共筛选出419篇文章,其中20项研究符合所有纳入标准。数据提取和质量评估采用牛津循证医学中心和新泽西-奥塔瓦量表标准。结果 在3505项临床相关检测中,汇总敏感度为80.3%(95% CI 70.9%-87.2%),特异度为95.5%(90.9%-97.8%)。对本研究的荟萃分析显示,根治性治疗治疗后复发的HPV阳性OPSCC总体患病率为9.70%(95% CI 8.72%-10.78%)。在该患病率下,阴性预测值(NPV)为97.7%(96.7%-98.5%),阳性预测值(PPV)为66.0%(49.5%-80.3%)。根治性治疗治疗后ctDNA检测呈阳性结果的患者,其疾病复发的比值比(OR)为130.3(95% CI 56.60-298.71),显著高于阴性结果。结论 ctDNA是早期检测复发的有前景的生物标志物。需要标准化的协议和定量阈值以充分确立其在临床实践中的作用。

title: Lactobacillus Depletion and Cervicovaginal Dysbiosis in Human Papillomavirus Persistence and Cervical Lesion Outcomes: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis will investigate whether alterations in the cervicovaginal microbiome are associated with the persistence or clearance of human papillomavirus (HPV) infection and with the subsequent clinical course of cervical lesions. Particular emphasis will be placed on Lactobacillus depletion, loss of Lactobacillus dominance, Lactobacillus species composition, community state types, microbial diversity, bacterial vaginosis, and the enrichment of potentially pathogenic or anaerobic bacterial taxa. The review will primarily include longitudinal observational studies involving women or adolescent females with repeated HPV testing and/or follow-up assessment of cervical intraepithelial lesions. Eligible outcomes will include type-specific or high-risk HPV persistence and clearance, acquisition of new HPV infection, and the persistence, progression, regression, or recurrence of cervical cytological or histological abnormalities. Studies evaluating microbiome-modifying or lesion-directed interventions will be considered separately as treatment-associated cohorts and will not be combined uncritically with untreated observational populations. Where sufficient clinical and methodological homogeneity exists, quantitative synthesis will estimate associations between cervicovaginal microbial characteristics and HPV or cervical lesion outcomes. Molecular microbiome studies, targeted analyses of specific bacterial taxa, and studies using clinical indicators of vaginal microecology or bacterial vaginosis will be analysed in prespecified categories. Sources of heterogeneity will be explored according to microbiome assessment method, HPV genotype, follow-up duration, population characteristics, HIV status, vaccination status, treatment exposure, and cervical disease severity. The anticipated outcome is a rigorous synthesis of the longitudinal evidence concerning the prognostic significance of cervicovaginal dysbiosis in HPV-related disease. The findings may help identify microbial biomarkers for risk stratification, clarify priorities for future prospective research, and inform the development of microbiome-based monitoring or therapeutic strategies.

abstract_zh: 本系统综述与元分析将探讨宫颈阴道菌群的变化是否与人乳头瘤病毒(人乳头瘤病毒)感染的持续或清除以及随后的宫颈病变临床过程相关。特别关注Lactobacillus缺乏、Lactobacillus优势丧失、Lactobacillus种群组成、菌群状态类型、微生物多样性、细菌性阴道病以及潜在致病性或厌氧菌类群的富集。综述将主要纳入涉及女性或青少年女性的纵向观察性研究,这些研究包含重复的人乳头瘤病毒检测或宫颈上皮内瘤变的随访评估。合格的结局包括特定型别或高危型HPV的持续或清除、新的人乳头瘤病毒感染获得,以及宫颈细胞学或组织学异常的持续、进展、消退或复发。评估微生物群修饰或病变导向干预的研究将被单独归类为治疗相关队列研究,并不会未经批判地与未治疗的观察人群合并分析。在临床和方法学上存在足够同质性的情况下,定量综合分析将估计宫颈阴道微生物特征与人乳头瘤病毒或宫颈病变结局之间的关联。分子微生物群研究、特定细菌类群的靶向分析以及使用阴道微生态或细菌性阴道病临床指标的研究将被预先设定的类别进行分析。异质性的来源将根据微生物群评估方法、人乳头瘤病毒基因型、随访时间、人群特征、HIV状态、疫苗接种状态、治疗暴露和宫颈疾病严重程度进行探讨。预期结果是对与人乳头瘤病毒相关疾病中宫颈阴道菌群失调的预后意义的纵向证据进行严谨的综合分析。研究结果可能有助于识别微生物生物标志物以进行风险分层,明确未来前瞻性研究的优先事项,并为基于微生物群的监测或治疗策略的发展提供信息。

title: Associations of temperature, particulate matter, and greenness with human papillomavirus positivity at screening: an analysis of Guangdong Province (2016–2022) using the treed distributed lag nonlinear model
abstract: Introduction Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a double-stranded DNA virus that may cause cervical, vulvar, and anal cancers in women. Environmental factors including temperature, air pollution, and greenness may be associated with HPV positivity; however, evidence remains limited. Methods This study analysed health examination data of 1,287,412 women in Guangdong Province, China (2016-2022). Ten covariates were collected, and temperature, particulate matter 2.5 (PM2.5), and normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) were assigned by examination date. Tree distributed lag non-linear models were applied to evaluate lagged associations with HPV positivity at screening. Results Using the Q50 of biweekly mean temperature, PM2.5, and NDVI (25.594°C, 20.300 μg/m3, and 0.544, respectively) as references, low temperature (Q2.5, 13.300°C) was associated with higher cumulative odds of HPV positivity at Lag Weeks 3-8 (cOR = 1.303, 95% CrI, 1.194, 1.428), whereas high temperature (Q97.5, 29.851°C) showed a longer-lag association at Lag Weeks 9-14 (cOR = 1.063, 95% CrI, 1.007, 1.122). High PM2.5 (Q97.5, 38.021μg/m3) and low NDVI (Q2.5, 0.229) were associated with higher odds of HPV positivity over Lag Weeks 1-16 (cOR = 1.172, 95% CrI, 1.051, 1.283) and Lag Weeks 5-18 (cOR = 1.318, 95% CrI, 1.131, 1.566), respectively. Stratified analyses suggested stronger low-temperature associations among middle-aged and older women and among women in the Pearl River Delta and Western Guangdong. Discussion In conclusion, temperature showed lag-dependent associations with screening-detected HPV positivity, with stronger associations for low temperature at shorter lags and high temperature at longer lags. High PM2.5 and low NDVI were also associated with higher odds in the primary 24-week analyses. Temporal sensitivity analyses attenuated the PM2.5 association and weakened the NDVI association under the 36-week specification, whereas the low-temperature association was comparatively stable and uncertainty increased for high temperature. These findings identify pre-screening environmental correlates of HPV positivity and warrant confirmation in longitudinal studies with repeated HPV testing and more comprehensive control of temporal, spatial, behavioral, and socioeconomic factors.

title: Impact of menopausal status on human papillomavirus detection and cervical neoplasia in middle-aged Senegalese women
abstract: Hormonal and immunologic changes related to menopause may play a role in human papillomavirus (HPV) and cervical neoplasia detection, yet this relationship has not been examined in West African populations, where cervical cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related death. The purpose of this study was to assess whether menopausal status is associated with HPV and cervical neoplasia detection in Senegalese women aged 40–60. We conducted a secondary analysis of three prospective cervical cancer studies in Dakar, Senegal (1998–2011). Participants with known menopausal status and a satisfactory HPV test (N = 3,118) and/or Pap smear (N = 2,907) were included, excluding those with cervical cancer or pregnancy; participants without known HIV status were additionally excluded from the cervical neoplasia analysis. Multivariable logistic regression and generalized estimating equations were used to estimate adjusted odds ratios and 95% confidence intervals, adjusting for age, gravidity, and HIV status. Compared with premenopausal women, postmenopausal women had significantly higher odds of HPV detection (OR = 1.48; 95% CI: 1.18, 1.85), including both high-risk (OR = 1.55; 95% CI: 1.25, 1.93) and low-risk types (OR = 1.64; 95% CI: 1.30, 2.08). Odds of cervical neoplasia were elevated, but non-significant, among postmenopausal women (OR = 1.36; 95% CI: 0.97, 1.90), with increased odds for both high-grade (OR = 1.43; 95% CI: 0.90, 2.28) and low-grade lesions (OR = 1.30; 95% CI: 0.84, 2.02). However, in a sensitivity analysis restricted to participants with known HIV status, these cervical neoplasia odds were attenuated, suggesting caution in interpreting the magnitude of these findings. These findings suggest menopause may contribute to HPV persistence or reactivation, and development of cervical neoplasia. Our results highlight the importance of continued surveillance for HPV and cervical neoplasia among older women, particularly in low-resource settings with disproportionately high cervical cancer burden.

title: Association of Receipt of Human Papillomavirus Vaccination and Personal History of Cancer Diagnosis in the United States: A Cross-Sectional Study Using NHIS Data
abstract: Background: Cancer survivors are at increased risk for developing subsequent cancers, including HPV-associated cancers, compared to the general population. However, evidence regarding the receipt of HPV vaccination and cancer diagnosis status is limited. Methods: We analyzed 2019 and 2022 National Health Interview Survey data, focusing on adults aged 18–45 years who were eligible for HPV vaccination. title: A Multimethod Evaluation to Assess Feasibility, Acceptability, and Preliminary Efficacy of HPVVaxFacts, a Tailored Mobile Web App, for Parents With Unvaccinated Children: Pilot 2-Arm Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: Abstract Background Mobile health (mHealth) interventions may improve provider-parent communication on human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination to reduce concerns, and increase intention and uptake. HPVVaxFacts (233 Analytics) is a novel, mobile web app delivering tailored education based on the Health Belief Model and Theory of Reasoned Action, addressing parental concerns preclinic visit. Objective This study aimed to assess the feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary efficacy of HPVVaxFacts among parents of adolescents aged 9‐17 years. Methods We conducted a pilot, randomized controlled trial in 2 urban Tennessee clinics from June to September 2023 comparing 2 groups: tailored education via HPVVaxFacts mobile web app (intervention, n=27), and nutrition education (attention control, n=30). Eligible parents had or were caregivers to a child aged 9 to 17 years unvaccinated against HPV, had a mobile phone, had an upcoming clinic visit, and spoke English. The recruitment strategy was patient intake software—Phreesia (Phreesia, Inc ) and eClinicalWorks (eClinicalWorks). Although unblinded, parents could deduce their study arm assignment. Providers were blinded. Feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary efficacy (HPV vaccine knowledge, concerns, intentions, and vaccination rates) were assessed using multimethod evaluation. Parents were assessed at baseline and immediately post intervention via surveys. Vaccination rates were assessed at 12 months post intervention via electronic health records. Nineteen parent interviews were conducted up to 9 months post intervention. A clinic staff consultation (n=6) was 1 month post intervention. Results Of 57 enrolled parents, most were female (52/57, 91%), non-Hispanic White (44/57, 77%), had ≤US $80,000 household income (32/57, 56%), and had some college or less (27/57, 47%). In total, 81% (36) of parents viewed HPVVaxFacts. Post intervention, HPV vaccine initiation was higher in the intervention group compared to the attention control group (48% vs 17%; difference 0.24; 95% CI 0.03-0.46; P =.01). Parents in the HPVVaxFacts arm demonstrated a greater reduction in knowledge (ie, knowledge increase; mean change: −0.6 vs 0.1) and concern scores (mean change: −3.4 vs −1.4) than those in the nutrition education arm. However, between-arm differences were not statistically significant ( P =.13 and P =.14, respectively). The majority found the study protocol and HPVVaxFacts acceptable. Benefits of HPVVaxFacts include confirming their decision to vaccinate, supporting parent-child discussion on the vaccine, and answering questions preclinic visit or offering questions for the provider. Study protocol delivery and mobile web app instructions were suggested areas for improvement. Barriers for HPVVaxFacts use include content in English only and digital format. Conclusions Our study suggests HPVVaxFacts was feasible and acceptable among parents to provide previsit, tailored information on HPV vaccination. Outcomes offer a positive trajectory but need more exploration. Next steps include a well-powered efficacy trial to determine the impact of HPVVaxFacts on initiation vaccine rates and parental hesitancy factors, as well as to explore an interaction, effect modification, and mediation among different variables.

title: Serum, cell-free, HPV-human DNA junction detection and HPV typing for predicting and monitoring cervical cancer recurrence.
abstract: Almost all cervical cancers are caused by human papillomaviruses (HPVs). In most cases, HPV DNA is integrated into the human genome. We found that tumor-specific, HPV-human DNA junctions are detectable in serum cell-free DNA of a fraction of cervical cancer patients at the time of initial treatment and/or at 6 months following treatment. Retrospective analysis revealed these junctions were more frequently detectable in women in whom the cancer later recurred. We also found that cervical cancers caused by HPV types outside of phylogenetic clade α9 had a higher recurrence frequency than those caused by α9 types in both our study and The Cancer Genome Atlas cervical cancer database, despite the higher prevalence ofα9 types, including HPV16, in cervical cancer. Thus, HPV-human DNA junction detection in serum cell-free DNA and HPV type determination in tumor tissue may help predict recurrence risk. Screening serum cell-free DNA for junctions may also offer an unambiguous non-invasive means to monitor absence of recurrence following treatment.

source_records.abstract: eLife AssessmentThis is a valuable study that suggests that HPV-human DNA junctions can be identified from cfDNA in women with cervical cancer and that detection of these junctions is indicative of recurrence.The evidence supporting the conclusions is incomplete, in part because the numbers of reads identifying breakpoints in tumor samples or in circulating cell-free serum samples are not provided.More quantitative analysis will be required to confirm that the breakpoints represented in cell-free DNA can be used as a surrogate to monitor the recurrence of cervical cancer cells, and additional patient studies would also be needed to strengthen the study.This work will be of interest to those who study and treat cervical cancer as well as other HPV-related malignancies.

title: Predictors of anal and cervical cancer screening uptake among adults with and without HIV: survey of a community-based health clinic network.
abstract: PURPOSE: People with HIV (PWH) in the United States (U.S.) are disproportionately impacted by human papillomavirus-related cancers. We aimed to identify sociodemographic, health, and social predictors of anal and cervical cancer screening uptake among adults with and without HIV. METHODS: We implemented a cross-sectional survey between April and June 2024 among adult patients receiving care at a community-based clinic network (predominantly based in Florida, U.S.) that delivers HIV prevention and treatment services. Outcomes included any receipt of anal cancer screening and guideline-adherent receipt of cervical cancer screening among eligible participants. We computed adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) to identify multilevel predictors associated with screening uptake. RESULTS: Among the survey respondents, 412 (42%) were eligible for anal cancer screening and 294 (30%) for cervical cancer screening. Participants eligible for anal cancer screening included 88.8% living with HIV and 82.3% men. Men with HIV were more likely to receive anal cancer screening compared to men without HIV (aPR 1.57, 95% CI 1.08, 2.27). Among men with HIV, anal cancer screening uptake was associated with any precancer diagnosis and having three or more comorbidities. Women eligible for cervical cancer screening included 43.5% living with HIV. Women with HIV were less likely to receive guideline-adherent cervical cancer screening compared to women without HIV (aPR 0.60, 95% CI 0.47, 0.77). HIV-related disclosure concerns were associated with lower guideline-adherent cervical screening uptake among women with HIV (aPR 0.75, 95% CI 0.60, 0.94). CONCLUSION: Screening-eligible participants with HIV were more likely to receive anal cancer screening and less likely to receive cervical cancer screening. Anal and cervical cancer screening uptake differed among subpopulations of people with HIV, including by race/ethnicity, household size, any precancer, comorbidities, and HIV-related stigma. Efforts to improve anal and cervical cancer screening uptake among high-risk and screening-eligible populations are needed.

title: Randomised phase III trials of cancer prevention drugs: a systematic review and prediction of trial success.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Pharmacological cancer risk reduction has received far less investment than therapeutic oncology and only a few agents have entered routine practice. Understanding the predictors of positive outcomes of previous trials and issues faced is critical to future developments. METHODS: This systematic review (PROSPERO CRD420250650276) included all phase III randomised controlled trials enrolling cancer-free adults over the past 45 years, evaluating pharmacological agents and whose primary or major secondary endpoint was directly related to cancer risk reduction. To predict trials' 'success', defined here as meeting the prespecified cancer risk reduction-related endpoint within the planned timeline, we used the Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator followed by multivariable logistic regression. RESULTS: Ninety-two trials comprising 659 904 participants were included, of which 46 (50.0%) met their primary endpoint. Success rates varied by therapeutic class: vitamins (9 of 38, 23.7%), endocrine therapies (15 of 20, 75.0%), nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (8 of 13, 61.5%), human papillomavirus vaccines (8 of 9, 88.9%) and anti-infective agents (5 of 8, 62.5%). Proportionally, breast (76.5%), cervical (72.7%) and oesophagogastric (58.3%) cancer risk reduction trials had the highest success rates versus 23.7% for vitamins trials. Adherence was highest for vaccines [median 95%, interquartile range (IQR) 93%-96%] and lowest for endocrine therapies (median 70%, IQR 65%-78%). Major safety issues arising for a dozen of the drugs limited their approval (n = 5) and use. In the multivariable analysis, the odds of success increased for trials with pharmaceutical sponsorship [odds ratio (OR) 5.30, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.01-35.77] and decreased for non mechanism-specific drugs and for studies with lower pretrial evidence (OR 0.30, 95% CI 0.10-0.90). CONCLUSIONS: Although half of the pharmacological cancer risk reduction trials conducted so far have shown positive results, only a handful have led to regulatory approval. Trial success was driven by more targeted strategies and strong preliminary evidence, underscoring the need for mechanism-driven, strong-evidence development pathways in cancer risk reduction.

title: Integrating Cervical Cancer Prevention into HIV Services in Sub-Saharan Africa: A Narrative Review Addressing the Dual Burden Among Women.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Women with HIV face a higher risk of cervical cancer. This review synthesizes evidence on precancerous cervical lesions among women with HIV in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), regional differences, risk factors, and approaches to integrating cervical cancer prevention into HIV services. METHODS: We conducted a comprehensive literature search across PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science databases through December 2025 and identified studies evaluating the prevalence of precancerous cervical lesions among women with HIV in SSA. It highlights prevalence, ongoing global efforts, and integration strategies specific to SSA. RESULTS: The prevalence of precancerous cervical lesions among women with HIV in SSA is higher in Tanzania (71.8%), and Kenya (42%), eastern countries than from western (Nigeria, 26.6%) or southern countries (South Africa, 23.2%), influenced by the distribution of human papillomavirus (HPV) genotypes, including higher-risk HPV (HR-HPV) such as HPV 35, which is not targeted by the HPV vaccine. CONCLUSIONS: Given the increased risk among women with HIV and the substantial burden in SSA, evidence suggests that integrating HPV-based cervical cancer screening and vaccination into HIV care platforms could help close the prevention gap and reduce the dual burden among women with HIV in SSA.

title_zh: 将 宫颈癌 预防纳入撒哈拉以南非洲的艾滋病毒服务:解决妇女双重负担的叙述性审查。
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Women with HIV face a higher risk of cervical cancer. This review synthesizes evidence on precancerous cervical lesions among women with HIV in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), regional differences, risk factors, and approaches to integrating cervical cancer prevention into HIV services. METHODS: We conducted a comprehensive literature search across PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science databases through December 2025 and identified studies evaluating the prevalence of precancerous cervical lesions among women with HIV in SSA. It highlights prevalence, ongoing global efforts, and integration strategies specific to SSA. RESULTS: The prevalence of precancerous cervical lesions among women with HIV in SSA is higher in Tanzania (71.8%), and Kenya (42%), eastern countries than from western (Nigeria, 26.6%) or southern countries (South Africa, 23.2%), influenced by the distribution of human papillomavirus (HPV) genotypes, including higher-risk HPV (HR-HPV) such as HPV 35, which is not targeted by the HPV vaccine. CONCLUSIONS: Given the increased risk among women with HIV and the substantial burden in SSA, evidence suggests that integrating HPV-based cervical cancer screening and vaccination into HIV care platforms could help close the prevention gap and reduce the dual burden among women with HIV in SSA.
abstract_zh: 背景:感染 HIV 的女性面临更高的 宫颈癌 风险。本综述综合了撒哈拉以南非洲 (SSA) 感染艾滋病毒的妇女中宫颈癌前病变的证据、区域差异、危险因素以及将 宫颈癌 预防纳入艾滋病毒服务的方法。方法:我们对截至 2025 年 12 月的 PubMed、Embase、Scopus 和 Web of Science 数据库进行了全面的文献检索,并确定了评估 SSA 感染 HIV 女性宫颈癌前病变 患病率 的研究。它重点介绍了 患病率、持续的全球努力以及针对 SSA 的集成策略。结果:SSA 感染 HIV 的女性中,坦桑尼亚 (71.8%) 和肯尼亚 (42%) 等东部国家的宫颈癌前病变 患病率 高于西方国家 (尼日利亚,26.6%) 或南部国家 (南非,23.2%),这受到 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 基因型分布的影响,包括高危 HPV (HR-HPV),例如 HPV 35,不是 HPV 疫苗 的目标。结论:鉴于感染艾滋病毒的女性风险增加以及 SSA 的沉重负担,有证据表明,将基于 HPV 的 宫颈癌 筛查和 疫苗接种 纳入艾滋病毒护理平台可以帮助缩小预防差距,并减轻 SSA 感染艾滋病毒的女性的双重负担。

title: Protect her future: Lessons learned from a school and community engagement initiative for HPV vaccine awareness in Lilongwe, Malawi.
abstract: ABSTRACT Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is an effective strategy for preventing cervical cancer, yet vaccine uptake in Malawi remains low because of misinformation, limited awareness, and parental hesitancy. This study describes the implementation of a youth-led school and community engagement initiative to promote HPV vaccine awareness in Lilongwe, Malawi, and highlights lessons for future immunization programs. We conducted a descriptive implementation case study of a two-day youth-led engagement initiative coordinated by fellows of the 2025–2026 Global Health Corps Malawi Leadership Accelerator in collaboration with the Lilongwe District Health Office, Kawale Primary School, and partner organizations. Activities included stakeholder meetings, school health education, myth-busting sessions, learner-centered activities, community dialogs, distribution of educational materials, and on-site HPV vaccination services. Girls aged 9–14y were the primary vaccination beneficiaries, while parents, caregivers, teachers, religious leaders, and community stakeholders were engaged to strengthen vaccine acceptance. Implementation data were collected through attendance records, field notes, dialogue summaries, and reflections. Descriptive statistics and qualitative content analysis were used. The initiative reached over 500 adolescent girls through school awareness activities and engaged 45 community stakeholders across six sites. Two community dialogue sessions were conducted, 1,000 educational materials distributed, and 100 eligible girls received HPV vaccination. Community discussions identified concerns about fertility, vaccine safety, and gender targeting, while trust in health workers, school involvement, participatory dialogue, and community leader support facilitated engagement. Youth-led, community-centered engagement highlighted lessons for improving HPV vaccination through addressing misinformation, building trust, and strengthening health system readiness.

title_zh: 保护她的未来:从马拉维利隆圭学校和社区参与 HPV 疫苗 意识活动中汲取的经验教训。
source_body_en: ABSTRACT Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is an effective strategy for preventing cervical cancer, yet vaccine uptake in Malawi remains low because of misinformation, limited awareness, and parental hesitancy. This study describes the implementation of a youth-led school and community engagement initiative to promote HPV vaccine awareness in Lilongwe, Malawi, and highlights lessons for future immunization programs. We conducted a descriptive implementation case study of a two-day youth-led engagement initiative coordinated by fellows of the 2025–2026 Global Health Corps Malawi Leadership Accelerator in collaboration with the Lilongwe District Health Office, Kawale Primary School, and partner organizations. Activities included stakeholder meetings, school health education, myth-busting sessions, learner-centered activities, community dialogs, distribution of educational materials, and on-site HPV vaccination services. Girls aged 9–14y were the primary vaccination beneficiaries, while parents, caregivers, teachers, religious leaders, and community stakeholders were engaged to strengthen vaccine acceptance. Implementation data were collected through attendance records, field notes, dialogue summaries, and reflections. Descriptive statistics and qualitative content analysis were used. The initiative reached over 500 adolescent girls through school awareness activities and engaged 45 community stakeholders across six sites. Two community dialogue sessions were conducted, 1,000 educational materials distributed, and 100 eligible girls received HPV vaccination. Community discussions identified concerns about fertility, vaccine safety, and gender targeting, while trust in health workers, school involvement, participatory dialogue, and community leader support facilitated engagement. Youth-led, community-centered engagement highlighted lessons for improving HPV vaccination through addressing misinformation, building trust, and strengthening health system readiness.

title: Societal and fiscal gains from HPV vaccination in Poland - return on investment from extending access to HPV vaccination.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the societal and fiscal impact of extending the current human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination program in Poland (boys and girls aged 9-14 with average 20% vaccine coverage) by expanding age eligibility (9-17 years) and increasing vaccination coverage. METHODS: A cost-benefit analysis was conducted from both a macroeconomic (societal) and public economic (fiscal) perspective. A dynamic transmission model (DTM) was used to project the incidence and mortality of HPV-related diseases over a 100-year time horizon. Epidemiological outcomes were translated into economic outcomes using societal and fiscal frameworks incorporating productivity losses, tax revenues, and healthcare costs, and were compared with incremental vaccination costs. All costs and benefits were discounted at an annual rate of 3%. RESULTS: Compared with the current national immunization program, extending vaccination to boys and girls aged 9-17 and increasing coverage to 60% is projected to result in incremental reductions of 16% in HPV-related diseases and 13% in deaths. Achieving 90% coverage was associated with reductions of 33% in HPV-related diseases and 27% in deaths. These health gains are estimated to translate into societal benefits of EUR 4.5 billion and EUR 9.8 billion, and fiscal benefits of EUR 2.4 billion and EUR 5.1 billion, under the 60% and 90% coverage scenarios, respectively. Incremental vaccination costs are estimated at EUR 1.1 billion and EUR 2.1 billion for respective coverage scenarios. The benefit-cost analysis indicates that every EUR 1 invested yields returns of EUR 4.2 (societal) and EUR 2.2 (fiscal) at 60% coverage, and EUR 4.6 (societal) and EUR 2.4 (fiscal) at 90% coverage. All results represent incremental gains relative to the existing program. CONCLUSION: Expanding HPV vaccination eligibility and coverage in Poland is expected to generate substantial societal and fiscal returns. Higher vaccination coverage not only reduces the burden of HPV-related diseases and associated mortality but also delivers a strong and sustainable return on investment.
